classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed local rate of Coulomb-collisional energy transfer per unit volume to a specified fast-ion species, summed over all ionic charge states without an orbit-class restriction.
items.documentation: Fast-ion collisional power density is the signed local rate at which Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to the nonthermal population of a specified ion species. It is an energy source or sink for the receiving fast ions, not their stored kinetic-energy density or the collisional heating delivered to bulk thermal ions. The defining kinetic-energy moment is $$ P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_q \sum_b \int \frac{1}{2}m_i |\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{iq,b}[f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}},f_b](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $P_{i,\mathrm{fast}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the fast-ion collisional power density, $i$ identifies the receiving ion species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states, $b$ labels the designated collision partners, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $m_i$ is the receiving ion mass. The function $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the fast-ion velocity distribution for charge state $q$, $f_b$ is the collision-partner distribution, and $C_{iq,b}$ is the Coulomb collision operator giving the collisional time derivative of the receiving distribution due to that partner. The receiving population is summed over all ionic charge states and includes all guiding-center orbit classes. Contributions from multiple distributions representing the fast-ion population are additive. The partner sum includes only the designated exchanges and reduces to one contribution when a single distribution species supplies the collision partner. This quantity is spatially local; neither a magnetic-flux-surface average nor a volume integral is implied. The [co-passing](name:co_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) and [counter-passing](name:counter_passing_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) variants restrict the contributing particle distribution, whereas the [trapped fast-ion variant](name:trapped_fast_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions) restricts the receiving population to trapped fast ions. The related [fast-ion charge-state collisional power density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions) resolves an ion collision-partner charge state; that partner resolution is distinct from summing the receiving species over charge states here. This quantity supplies a fast-population contribution to [ion collisional power density](name:ion_power_density_due_to_collisions). Summing the fast-ion contributions over the included ion species and adding the corresponding thermal-ion contributions gives the aggregate ion collisional power density. Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions increase the kinetic-energy density of the receiving fast-ion population.

items.name: incident_neutral_particle_flux_at_wall
items.description: Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated arrival rate of neutral particles of one specified species moving from the plasma side toward plasma-facing material. It excludes neutral particles emitted by the wall.
items.documentation: Incident neutral particle flux at the wall is the wall-integrated rate at which neutral particles of one specified species arrive at plasma-facing material from the plasma side. It counts incoming neutral particles crossing the material boundary toward the wall, not particles emitted by the wall. The wall-integrated arrival rate is the surface integral of the corresponding local incident flux: $$ \dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}} = \int_{A_\mathrm{wall}} \Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})\, dA $$ where $\dot{N}_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}$ denotes this incident neutral particle flux at the wall, $A_\mathrm{wall}$ is the plasma-facing wall surface included in the total, $\Gamma_{n,\mathrm{wall}}^{\mathrm{inc}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the incident component of the local neutral particle flux at the wall for the same neutral species at wall position $\mathbf{x}$, and $dA$ is the surface-area element. The quantity is species-resolved for one neutral species and aggregated over wall position by surface integration. It is not the local per-area neutral particle flux at the wall at a given wall position, and it is not a signed net balance between incoming and outgoing neutrals. Wall-emitted neutral particles belong to the opposite direction of exchange and are represented separately by quantities such as [neutral particle flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:neutral_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Contributions from disjoint wall regions add to form the global incident rate.

items.name: kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Kinetic-energy power flux density carried away from a plasma-facing surface by emitted particles, including ions and electrons and aggregated over species.
items.documentation: This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by particles emitted from a plasma-facing surface through sputtering, reflection, secondary emission, or related surface-emission processes. It includes all emitted particle species and charge states, rather than selecting a particular ion or charge state. The kinetic-energy flux density is defined by $$ q_{\mathrm{kin}} = \sum_s \int_{\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}>0} \frac{1}{2}m_s v^2\,(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{n}) f_s(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $s$ indexes emitted particle species and charge states, $m_s$ is particle mass in kg, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity in m/s, $v=|\mathbf{v}|$, $\mathbf{n}$ is the outward surface-normal unit vector, and $f_s$ is the emitted-particle velocity distribution. The outward condition excludes particles incident on the surface. This is the kinetic component of [energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), excluding particle potential-energy contributions and photon or other radiative energy; [ion charge-state kinetic energy flux at wall due to surface emission](name:ion_charge_state_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission) is a charge-state-resolved instance.

items.name: toroidal_neutral_internal_state_torque_density
items.description: Toroidal component of the angular-momentum source density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
items.documentation: This quantity is the toroidal component of the torque density transferred to the plasma by neutral particles occupying a specified internal state. It is the state-resolved toroidal projection of neutral internal-state torque density, rather than a sum over all neutral internal states. $$ \tau_{\phi,s}=\hat{\phi}\cdot\left(\mathbf{r}\times\mathbf{f}_s\right) $$ where $\tau_{\phi,s}$ is the toroidal torque density, $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal unit vector in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector relative to the machine symmetry axis, and $\mathbf{f}_s$ is the force density exerted on the plasma by neutrals in internal state $s$. Summing this state-resolved quantity over all neutral internal states gives [toroidal neutral torque density](name:toroidal_neutral_torque_density); it is distinct from the direction-independent [neutral torque density](name:neutral_torque_density). Sign convention: Positive when the torque points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_reciprocating_probe
items.description: Toroidal angular coordinate of the reciprocating probe’s average measurement position during a plunge, referenced to the facility’s toroidal-angle origin.
items.documentation: The toroidal coordinate $\bar{\phi}_{\rm probe}$ identifies the azimuthal location of the reciprocating probe’s average position formed from its measurement locations. It is an angular coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. For an averaged position represented in the right-handed Cartesian $(x,y,z)$ basis, with $z$ aligned with $Z$, the coordinate is defined by $$ \\bar{\\phi}_{\\rm probe} = \\operatorname{atan2}(\\bar{y}_{\\rm probe}, \\bar{x}_{\\rm probe}) $$ where $\\bar{x}_{\\rm probe}$ and $\\bar{y}_{\\rm probe}$ are the Cartesian coordinates of the averaged position. This identifies the probe location analogously to the toroidal coordinate at a [beam tracing point](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_beam_tracing_point), but the locus here is the reciprocating probe’s average position. Sign convention: Positive when $\\bar{\\phi}_{\\rm probe}$ increases in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\\phi$.

items.name: toroidal_argon_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Toroidal component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame of the argon-ion bulk-flow velocity at the last closed flux surface.
items.documentation: This quantity is the local toroidal component of the argon-ion bulk-flow velocity evaluated at the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed flux surface. It is a pointwise boundary value rather than an average over that flux surface. The charge-state-aggregated toroidal velocity is defined by $$ V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi} = \frac{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z} v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}}{\sum_z n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}} $$ where $V_{\mathrm{Ar},\phi}$ and $v_{\mathrm{Ar},z,\phi}$ are toroidal velocity components in m s$^{-1}$, $n_{\mathrm{Ar},z}$ is the argon-ion number density in m$^{-3}$, and $z$ indexes argon ion charge states. The toroidal component is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The local value is distinct from the toroidal flux-surface-averaged argon velocity at the plasma boundary, which averages the same component over the boundary flux surface. Neutral argon is excluded from the ion bulk-flow aggregation. Sign convention: Positive when the argon-ion bulk velocity projects onto the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature
items.description: Dimensionless ratio comparing a particle species’ kinetic temperature with the positive reference temperature on the same magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: The quantity expresses the kinetic temperature of a selected particle species relative to a single reference thermal scale on the same magnetic flux surface. It is the normalized counterpart of [particle temperature](name:particle_temperature), while retaining the species dependence of the numerator. It is defined by $$ T_p^{\mathrm{norm}} = \frac{T_p}{T_{\mathrm{ref}}} $$ where $T_p$ is the kinetic temperature of the selected particle species and $T_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the positive reference temperature for the flux surface. The ratio is dimensionless and is not an absolute temperature; its value depends on the specified reference temperature.

items.name: upper_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module
items.description: Upper thickness of a breeder blanket module is the non-negative geometric separation through the upper cap, measured normal to its exterior boundary and main-body interface.
items.documentation: Upper thickness of a breeder blanket module is the geometric thickness of the cap that closes the module at its upper end. The reference surfaces are the upper exterior boundary of the cap and the interface where the upper cap joins the main module body. It is the top-cap poloidal thickness in a poloidal $(R,Z)$ section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is distinct from the overall thickness of a breeder blanket module and the corresponding [lower thickness of a breeder blanket module](name:lower_thickness_of_breeder_blanket_module). The upper-cap thickness is the normal projection of the separation between the reference surfaces: $$ t_{\mathrm{upper}} = \left|\left(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ext}} - \mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{int}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\right| $$ where $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ and $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{int}}$ are corresponding points on the upper exterior boundary and cap-to-body interface, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the local unit normal directed through the upper cap in the poloidal section, and $t_{\mathrm{upper}}$ is the upper-cap thickness. The quantity applies to one breeder blanket module and is not summed or averaged over modules. It is a non-negative geometric magnitude; it is not a signed coordinate, vertical height, or displacement and excludes the thicknesses of internal breeder, coolant, or shielding layers.

items.name: parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized parallel diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient.
items.documentation: The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient $D_{i,z,E,\parallel}$ quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in one specified charge state $z$ along the magnetic field. It is the parallel component of the direction-agnostic [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient). The defining relation for the density-normalized parallel diffusive energy flux is: $$ \frac{Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,\parallel}\,\nabla_{\parallel} T_{i,z} $$ where $Q_{i,z,\parallel,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the parallel diffusive thermal-energy flux of charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is its number density, $T_{i,z}$ is its temperature, and $\nabla_{\parallel}$ is the derivative along the magnetic-field direction. This coefficient applies to one specified ion charge state and is not summed over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions; the broader [parallel ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) represents the corresponding transport aggregated over ion species.

items.name: length_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description: Physical extent of a poloidal magnetic-field probe coil measured along its assigned local normal sensing axis, contributing to the coil’s magnetic-flux response.
items.documentation: The length of a poloidal magnetic-field probe is the physical extent of its sensing coil along the coil’s assigned local normal sensing axis. It describes the coil geometry rather than the length of a signal lead or the distance between mounting points. This quantity applies to one poloidal magnetic-field probe coil as a whole. It is distinct from the [area of the poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:area_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), which describes the area enclosed by one winding turn, and from the [turn count of the poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe), which describes the number and orientation of complete turns. The coil length, its enclosed per-turn area, and its winding-turn count jointly characterize the probe’s magnetic-flux coupling and effective sensing geometry. The length does not itself specify the coil area, winding count, or magnetic-field orientation.

items.name: iron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier, summed over all iron ion charge states and excluding neutral iron.
items.documentation: Particle number density of iron ions evaluated on the flux surface assigned to an internal transport barrier is the local density of the iron-ion population at that flux-surface location. It is the iron-specific member of the [density at the internal transport barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier) family. Iron has atomic number $Z=26$. The number density is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{Fe}} = \lim_{\Delta V\to 0}\frac{\Delta N_{\mathrm{Fe}}}{\Delta V} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the iron-ion number density, $N_{\mathrm{Fe}}$ is the number of counted iron ions, and $V$ is volume. The count is summed over all iron ionic charge states and excludes neutral iron. The internal transport barrier is the designated flux-surface location where reduced cross-field turbulent transport can sustain steep impurity-density gradients, as for [carbon density at the internal transport barrier](name:carbon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier).

items.name: normalized_particle_charge
items.description: Dimensionless charge number of a particle species, obtained by dividing its physical charge by the positive reference charge used for normalization.
items.documentation: This quantity is the normalized form of particle charge for a particle species. It preserves the sign of the physical charge and expresses its magnitude relative to a common positive reference charge. The normalized charge is defined by $$ q_{\rm n} = \frac{q}{q_{\rm ref}} $$ where $q$ is the species' physical electric charge and $q_{\rm ref}$ is the strictly positive reference charge, both expressed in the same charge units. The result is dimensionless and is used as the charge-coupling coefficient in normalized electromagnetic and electrostatic equations. Its sign distinguishes positive and negative charge, while its magnitude gives the charge relative to the selected reference.

items.name: poloidal_electron_particle_flux
items.description: Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed net electron crossing rate per unit area perpendicular to the local poloidal direction around a plasma cross-section.
items.documentation: Poloidal electron particle flux is the signed net electron number flow per unit area normal to the local poloidal direction. It describes particle transport around a plasma cross-section, rather than transport along the toroidal direction or necessarily along the magnetic field. The defining velocity moment is $$ \Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}) f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $\Gamma_{e,\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal electron particle flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron number-flux vector, $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the positive local poloidal unit tangent, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $f_e$ is the local electron velocity distribution normalized to electron number density, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The poloidal tangent lies in a constant-toroidal-angle cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Its positive orientation must be specified by the poloidal-direction convention. The integral includes the full electron velocity distribution, with opposite crossings contributing opposite signs. In the plasma edge, this remains a local flux density: neither surface integration nor flux-surface averaging is implied. This component specializes [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux) to an oriented surface whose normal is the poloidal unit tangent. It is a number flux, not an electric-charge flux; unlike [poloidal electron energy flux](name:poloidal_electron_energy_flux), it has no energy weighting. Sign convention: Positive when the net electron number flow follows the specified positive local poloidal tangent, independently of the negative electron charge.

items.name: derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate
items.description: Geometric rate at which the cumulative volume enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface changes with its dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate.
items.documentation: This quantity is the geometric derivative of the cumulative volume enclosed by a nested magnetic flux surface with respect to the dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate. It describes how rapidly the enclosed region expands as the flux-surface label changes. The defining relation is $$ \frac{dV}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}} $$ where $V$ is the [volume enclosed by a flux surface](name:volume_of_flux_surface) and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionful toroidal-flux coordinate labeling the nested surfaces. The quantity applies to the three-dimensional region inside each selected nested magnetic flux surface. The volume is cumulative, beginning at the magnetic axis and extending to the specified surface; this is not a local plasma-population quantity and carries no species weighting. It is the derivative with respect to the toroidal-flux coordinate, not the volume itself or the derivative of the enclosed poloidal area. As the derivative of [volume enclosed by a flux surface](name:volume_of_flux_surface), it provides the volume increment associated with a change in toroidal-flux coordinate and serves as a geometric coefficient in flux-surface-averaged transport relations. The derivative of area with respect to the toroidal-flux coordinate is the analogous area derivative, while [the temporal derivative of this volume derivative](name:time_derivative_of_derivative_of_volume_of_flux_surface_with_respect_to_toroidal_flux_coordinate) describes its change in time.

items.name: plasma_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination
items.description: Plasma-ion power deposited on a divertor target by recombination processes at the plasma-material interface, excluding the neutral-particle recombination channel.
items.documentation: This quantity captures the plasma-ion recombination power delivered to a single divertor target, representing energy deposited when plasma ions recombine at or near the plasma-material interface. It excludes the neutral-particle recombination channel quantified by [neutral-particle recombination power](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination). The plasma-ion contribution is obtained from the total target recombination power by subtracting the neutral-particle contribution: $$ P_{\rm plasma,target} = P_{\rm rec,target} - P_{\rm neutral,target} $$ where $P_{\rm plasma,target}$ is this plasma-ion recombination power, $P_{\rm rec,target}$ is the [total recombination power at the divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), and $P_{\rm neutral,target}$ is the neutral-particle contribution. This is the single-target plasma-ion component of recombination power, distinct from [total divertor recombination power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), which aggregates over all divertor target surfaces and includes both plasma-ion and neutral-particle channels.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Charge-state-summed krypton ion number density averaged over the complete separatrix, distinguishing a flux-surface value from the local boundary value.
items.documentation: The quantity is the charge-state-summed number density of krypton ions, averaged over the complete plasma-boundary separatrix. It represents krypton particle content associated with the last closed magnetic flux surface, rather than a pointwise value; the corresponding local quantity is the [krypton ion number density at the plasma boundary](name:krypton_density_at_plasma_boundary). The flux-surface average is defined by $$ \left\langle n_{\mathrm{Kr}} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS},b} = \frac{\displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}_b} n_{\mathrm{Kr}}\,\frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}} {\displaystyle\int_{\mathcal{S}_b} \frac{dS}{\lvert\nabla\psi\rvert}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the local krypton ion number density, $\mathcal{S}_b$ is the plasma-boundary separatrix, $dS$ is the surface-area element, and $\psi$ is the magnetic-flux surface label. All krypton ion charge states are included in $n_{\mathrm{Kr}}$; neutral krypton and any single-charge-state density are excluded.

items.name: ethane_source_rate
items.description: Instantaneous ethane-gas injection rate into the plasma vessel, expressed as equivalent electrons per second, with 18 equivalent electrons assigned to each neutral C2H6 molecule.
items.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous rate at which neutral ethane molecules are delivered to the plasma vessel, converted to an equivalent-electron rate. It counts the electrons associated with neutral molecular composition, not free electrons produced by ionization. $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=18\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}(t) $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_2H_6}}$ is the neutral ethane molecular injection rate in molecules per second, and $t$ is time in seconds. The factor $18=2\times6+6\times1$ is the total atomic-number electron count of one C2H6 molecule. This is an instantaneous rate rather than a cumulative inventory; its time integral gives the accumulated equivalent-electron count represented by [accumulated ethane count](name:accumulated_ethane_count). It excludes other molecular species, including the distinct [ethylene source rate](name:ethylene_source_rate).

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment
items.description: Azimuthal location of a shattered-pellet fragment’s center of mass around the machine symmetry axis, expressed in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the toroidal angle $\phi_f$ of a shattered-pellet fragment’s center of mass. It specifies that position around the machine symmetry axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ frame, whose coordinate values are $(R,\phi,Z)$; $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height. Using Cartesian coordinates $(x_f,y_f,z_f)$ of the same center of mass in the right-handed $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, the toroidal angle is $$ \phi_f = \operatorname{atan2}(y_f,x_f) $$ where $\operatorname{atan2}$ gives the oriented azimuth relative to the defined $\phi=0$ direction. The angle is periodic modulo $2\pi$ and is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate at the shattering position](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_shattering_position) and the [toroidal coordinate of the intact pellet](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet). Sign convention: Positive when the fragment center of mass lies in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side
items.description: Magnetic field at the pedestal top low-field side is the local magnetic induction vector evaluated at the low-field-side pressure-pedestal top. It retains radial, toroidal, and vertical field components in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame before component selection or magnitude reduction.
items.documentation: Magnetic field at the pedestal top low-field side is the local magnetic induction vector evaluated at the low-field-side top of the pressure pedestal. It gives the total field direction and strength at that locus in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, whose basis is $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ with $R$ the major-radius coordinate, $\phi$ the toroidal angle, and $Z$ the vertical coordinate. The vector is decomposed as $$ \mathbf{B}_\mathrm{ped,LFS} = B_R\hat{R} + B_\phi\hat{\phi} + B_Z\hat{Z} $$ where $\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{ped,LFS}$ is the magnetic-field vector at the low-field-side pressure-pedestal top, $B_R$ is its radial component, $B_\phi$ is its toroidal component, $B_Z$ is its vertical component, and $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$ is the right-handed cylindrical basis. The scope is locus-specific: it applies only at the low-field-side pressure-pedestal top, not throughout the pedestal, not at the pedestal foot or magnetic axis, and not as a spatial average over a flux surface or volume. The quantity has no species, charge-state, or particle-population aggregation; it is the electromagnetic field itself at the specified location. Relative to the unrestricted [magnetic field](name:magnetic_field), this quantity adds the pedestal-top low-field-side evaluation locus while retaining the same vector identity. Its child [magnetic-field magnitude at the pedestal top low-field side](name:magnetic_field_magnitude_at_pedestal_top_low_field_side) is the Euclidean norm $|\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{ped,LFS}| = \sqrt{B_R^2+B_\phi^2+B_Z^2}$ and therefore removes direction and component signs; individual component or projection names denote only the corresponding part of this vector. Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\mathbf{B}_\mathrm{ped,LFS}$ is directed along $+\hat{R}$, $+\hat{\phi}$, or $+\hat{Z}$, respectively, in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: width_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description: Full geometric width of a toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section, measured as the boundary-to-boundary transverse extent along the normal direction of the local Frenet-Serret frame. It is an unsigned extent, not a centerline location or coil radius.
items.documentation: Full geometric width of a toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section, measured along the normal axis of the local right-handed Frenet-Serret frame $(\hat{t}, \hat{n}, \hat{b})$. The tangent $\hat{t}$ follows the conductor centerline, the normal $\hat{n}$ lies in the cross-section plane, and the binormal $\hat{b} = \hat{t} \times \hat{n}$; the corresponding extent along $\hat{b}$ is [height_of_toroidal_field_coil](name:height_of_toroidal_field_coil). The width is the boundary-to-boundary span of the outer conductor boundary $\partial S$ projected onto $\hat{n}$: $$ w = \max_{\mathbf{r} \in \partial S} (\mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{n}) - \min_{\mathbf{r} \in \partial S} (\mathbf{r} \cdot \hat{n}) $$ where $\mathbf{r}$ is the position of a boundary point in the cross-section plane and $\hat{n}$ is the unit normal. Reversing the sense of $\hat{n}$ leaves $w$ unchanged, so it is an unsigned extent. For a rectangular or square section this is the full side length along $\hat{n}$; for a circular section it is the diameter; for an annular section it is the outer diameter, not the bore diameter or wall thickness. It is a geometric extent of the outer cross-section and is distinct from a centerline location or from a coil radius such as radius_of_toroidal_field_coil or [inner_radius_of_toroidal_field_coil](name:inner_radius_of_toroidal_field_coil).

items.name: accumulated_xenon_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown xenon inventory delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 54 count units assigned to each xenon atom.
items.documentation: This quantity is the cumulative inventory of xenon atoms introduced by gas injection after plasma breakdown, represented using an equivalent-electron counting convention. It denotes delivered xenon inventory rather than instantaneous xenon content in the plasma. The equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}} = Z_{\mathrm{Xe}} N_{\mathrm{Xe}} = 54 N_{\mathrm{Xe}} $$ where $N_{\mathrm{Xe,eq}}$ is the cumulative equivalent-electron xenon inventory, $Z_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon atomic number, and $N_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the cumulative number of xenon atoms delivered by post-breakdown gas injection. The scope is limited to xenon atoms delivered after plasma breakdown, with contributions from all post-breakdown gas-injection events cumulatively summed. No other injected species are included, and the quantity is not an instantaneous injection rate. The equivalent-electron convention uses the xenon atomic number and does not represent the actual number of free plasma electrons supplied by xenon; it is independent of the xenon ionization state. Gas introduced before breakdown is excluded and belongs to the distinct [accumulated xenon prefill inventory](name:accumulated_xenon_prefill_count), which provides the corresponding prefill contribution.

items.name: magnetic_field_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side
items.description: Magnetic field at the high-field-side pedestal top is the local total magnetic-induction vector evaluated at the high-field-side pressure-pedestal top. It retains field strength and direction before any component selection or magnitude reduction.
items.documentation: Magnetic field at the high-field-side pedestal top is the local total magnetic-induction vector evaluated at the high-field-side pressure-pedestal top. It includes all directional components of the local magnetic field at that locus and preserves both field strength and direction. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ major radius, $\phi$ toroidal angle, and $Z$ vertical height, the vector may be decomposed as $$ \mathbf{B} = B_R \hat{R} + B_\phi \hat{\phi} + B_Z \hat{Z} $$ where $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field at the high-field-side pedestal top, $B_R$, $B_\phi$, and $B_Z$ are its radial, toroidal, and vertical components at the same locus, and $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ are the corresponding unit basis vectors. The scope is restricted to the high-field-side branch of the pressure-pedestal top, not to arbitrary plasma positions or to the low-field-side pedestal top. The high-field side is the smaller-major-radius side in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where the toroidal magnetic-field magnitude is larger. The quantity is local at that locus; it is not a spatial average or a flux-surface average. This is a vector quantity, not the scalar [magnetic-field magnitude at the high-field-side pedestal top](name:magnetic_field_magnitude_at_pedestal_top_high_field_side), a single component, a projection, an absolute value, or a vacuum-field approximation. The scalar magnetic-field magnitude at the same locus is the Euclidean norm $|\mathbf{B}|$ of this vector and therefore removes directional information while retaining the shared high-field-side pedestal-top evaluation locus. Sign convention: Positive when a signed component of $\mathbf{B}$ points along the positive direction of the basis vector used for that component; in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame these directions are $+\hat{R}$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, and $+\hat{Z}$.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description: Major-radius coordinate locating the sphere center that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The quantity is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of the center of the sphere that defines an electron-cyclotron launcher mirror. It identifies the mirror's geometric reference point rather than a point on the reflecting surface. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, the major-radius coordinate relates to right-handed Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ through $$ R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2} $$ where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinate values in the $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity applies to the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror's spherical defining geometry and represents one geometric point. It is not a plasma quantity, a surface coordinate, a mirror steering angle, or an average or integral over the mirror. The broader [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) concept is specialized here to the sphere center of the mirror. Together with the [vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror) and [toroidal coordinate of the electron-cyclotron launcher mirror](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror), it locates the same geometric center.

items.name: radial_diamagnetic_current_density
items.description: Radial diamagnetic current density is the signed major-radius projection of pressure-gradient-driven electric current in the edge plasma.
items.documentation: Radial diamagnetic current density is the local major-radius projection of the pressure-gradient-driven contribution to [current density](name:current_density) in the edge plasma. It is a signed component of the vector [current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift). The projection is defined by: $$ j_{\mathrm{dia},R} = \hat{R}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}} $$ where $j_{\mathrm{dia},R}$ is the radial diamagnetic current density, $\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the diamagnetic current-density vector, and $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius measured from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This quantity includes the algebraic sum of diamagnetic contributions from all included charge carriers, without species or charge-state resolution. It excludes current contributions attributed to other mechanisms. The radial direction is the cylindrical major-radius direction, not a flux-surface-normal direction or the magnetic-field-perpendicular projection. The [diamagnetic current density](name:diamagnetic_current_density) is the magnitude of the same vector, whereas this component retains its directional sign. The [parallel diamagnetic current density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density) instead projects that vector onto the local magnetic-field direction. Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic conventional current flows toward increasing major radius $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: hydrogen_density
items.description: Local number density of hydrogen (protium) ions in the plasma, giving the count of H+ particles per unit volume at a specified spatial position.
items.documentation: The hydrogen density quantifies the local concentration of protium ions ($^1$H$^+$, the lightest hydrogen isotope with mass number $A = 1$) at a point in the plasma. It is distinct from the neutral atomic hydrogen density and from the number densities of heavier hydrogenic isotopes such as deuterium ($^2$H) and tritium ($^3$H). The number density $n_H$ at position $\mathbf{r}$ is defined as $$ n_H(\mathbf{r}) = \frac{dN_H}{dV} $$ where $N_H$ is the number of hydrogen ions within the infinitesimal volume element $dV$ centered at $\mathbf{r}$. Spatially averaged forms provide experimentally accessible measures of the same quantity: [line_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:line_averaged_hydrogen_density) gives the path-length-normalized ion count along a spectroscopic or interferometric chord, while [volume_averaged_hydrogen_density](name:volume_averaged_hydrogen_density) integrates the ion content over the full plasma volume. The isotopic composition of the hydrogenic fuel is tracked by [ratio_of_hydrogen_density_to_total_hydrogenic_density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_hydrogen_density_to_volume_averaged_total_hydrogenic_density), which expresses $n_H$ relative to the combined protium, deuterium, and tritium ion density. The aggregate over all three hydrogen isotopes is given by hydrogenic_density, and the full multi-species ion sum by [total_ion_density](name:total_ion_number_density).

items.name: momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless coefficient that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on momentum-flux density in multi-fluid edge plasma transport closures, capping the flux magnitude while leaving its sign direction unchanged.
items.documentation: In multi-fluid edge plasma transport models, gradient-driven diffusive closures can produce momentum-flux densities that exceed the physically realizable collisionless free-streaming limit in steep-gradient regions such as the scrape-off layer and divertor. A flux-limiter coefficient $\alpha_m$ is introduced to bound the effective flux: the limited momentum-flux density magnitude cannot exceed $\alpha_m$ times a free-streaming reference scale, while the sign follows the underlying diffusive flux direction. The limited momentum-flux density $\Pi^{\mathrm{lim}}$ is formed by the harmonic-mean combination: $$ \Pi^{\mathrm{lim}} = \frac{\alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} \cdot \Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}}{|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| + \alpha_m \, \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}} $$ where $\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the collisional diffusive momentum-flux estimate, $\Pi^{\mathrm{FS}} = m n v_{\mathrm{th}}^2$ is the free-streaming scale with $m$ the particle mass, $n$ the number density, and $v_{\mathrm{th}}$ the thermal speed. When $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \gg \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the flux saturates at $\pm \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$; when $|\Pi^{\mathrm{diff}}| \ll \alpha_m \Pi^{\mathrm{FS}}$ the diffusive value is recovered unchanged. Specializations target individual projection directions, such as parallel_momentum_coefficient for field-aligned transport, and individual particle populations, such as ion_state_momentum_coefficient for specific ion charge states or parallel_neutral_state_momentum_coefficient for neutral-particle parallel transport. The coefficient is intrinsically non-negative; values in the range 0.1–1 are common in edge-plasma simulations, selected by calibration against experimental separatrix and divertor data.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part
items.description: Real part of the single-toroidal-mode poloidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field, equal to the in-phase projection of the complex first-order vacuum magnetic-field perturbation onto the poloidal unit tangent outside the plasma.
items.documentation: Real part of the single-toroidal-mode poloidal perturbed vacuum magnetic field is the in-phase scalar component of the complex first-order vacuum magnetic-field perturbation projected onto the poloidal unit tangent outside the plasma. The poloidal unit tangent is defined in a specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$ as the direction of increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$, where $\phi$ is the toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame with basis $(\hat{R},\hat{\phi},\hat{Z})$. This poloidal direction is a local flux-coordinate tangent, not a cylindrical-basis direction. The real poloidal vacuum perturbation amplitude is defined by projecting the complex vacuum perturbation onto the poloidal unit tangent and taking the real part: $$ \delta B_{\theta,\mathrm{real}}^{\mathrm{vac}}(\rho,\theta;n) = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{vac}}(\rho,\theta;n) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}\right] $$ where $\delta B_{\theta,\mathrm{real}}^{\mathrm{vac}}$ is this real poloidal vacuum perturbation amplitude, $\delta\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the complex first-order [perturbed vacuum magnetic field](name:perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field) amplitude, $n$ is the integer toroidal mode number, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$ is the poloidal unit tangent defined above. The vacuum qualifier restricts the quantity to the current-free region exterior to the plasma, where the first-order perturbation satisfies $\nabla\times\delta\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{vac}}=0$ and $\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}^{\mathrm{vac}}=0$. For a single toroidal mode, the complex poloidal amplitude is reconstructed as $\delta B_{\theta}^{\mathrm{vac}}=\delta B_{\theta,\mathrm{real}}^{\mathrm{vac}}+i\,\delta B_{\theta,\mathrm{imag}}^{\mathrm{vac}}$ and enters the toroidal dependence through the factor $\exp(i n\phi)$; this quantity is the real part of that mode amplitude, not a poloidal Fourier coefficient. It is distinct from the [imaginary-part counterpart](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), the [radial](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) and [toroidal](name:toroidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part) vacuum projections, and the corresponding [plasma-region component](name:poloidal_perturbed_plasma_magnetic_field_real_part). Sign convention: Positive when the in-phase magnetic-field perturbation component points along $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\theta}$, the unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed $\rho$ and $\phi$ in the specified flux-coordinate system $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description: Squareness of a flux surface is the Luce (2013) shape coefficient for each nested closed magnetic flux surface, including the outer closed boundary when present, quantifying signed corner-sector departure from a reference ellipse in the poloidal cross-section. Positive values are box-like; negative values are diamond-like.
items.documentation: Squareness of a flux surface is the Luce (2013) shape coefficient that quantifies the signed departure of a nested closed magnetic-flux-surface contour from a reference ellipse in the corner sectors of its poloidal cross-section. Positive values describe box-like corner sectors relative to the reference ellipse, and negative values describe diamond-like or inward-pinched corner sectors. The contour is considered in a poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The quantity is defined separately for each member of the one-parameter family of nested closed flux surfaces, including the plasma boundary when it is the outer closed flux surface; it excludes open-field-line regions and material limiter, wall, or divertor surfaces. It is a contour-shape coefficient, not a flux-surface label, not a coordinate of the contour, not a boundary-only quantity, and not an average over neighboring flux surfaces. It captures corner departure from the reference ellipse; [elongation](name:elongation_of_flux_surface) captures the vertical stretching of the contour, and [triangularity](name:triangularity_of_flux_surface) captures the major-radius displacement of the upper and lower extrema. Sector-resolved squareness quantities use the same Luce reference-ellipse convention on named corner sectors: [upper outer squareness](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) on the upper-$Z$, larger-$R$ sector, [upper inner squareness](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) on the upper-$Z$, smaller-$R$ sector, [lower outer squareness](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) on the lower-$Z$, larger-$R$ sector, and [lower inner squareness](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) on the lower-$Z$, smaller-$R$ sector. [Outer squareness](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface) restricts the quantity to larger-$R$ corner sectors, [inner squareness](name:inner_squareness_of_flux_surface) restricts it to smaller-$R$ corner sectors, and [squareness of the plasma boundary](name:squareness_of_plasma_boundary) is the boundary specialization of the flux-surface quantity.

items.name: tungsten_density_at_divertor_target
items.description: Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary, summed over positive ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
items.documentation: Number density of tungsten ions at the divertor target is the local particle count per volume at the sheath entrance immediately upstream of the target-facing plasma boundary. It is the tungsten-specific member of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). The charge-state-summed tungsten number density is defined by $$ n_W = \sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{W^{Z+}} $$ where $n_W$ is the total local number density of tungsten ions, $n_{W^{Z+}}$ is the local number density of tungsten ions with positive charge state $Z$, and $Z$ is the integer tungsten ionization state from 1 through 74. This quantity applies only to tungsten ions immediately upstream of the electrostatic sheath at a divertor target. It includes every positive tungsten ionization state once, without charge-state weighting, and excludes neutral tungsten atoms and ions of all other elements. The charge-state sum makes this the species-level tungsten component of [density_at_divertor_target](name:density_at_divertor_target). Its divertor-target locus distinguishes it from [tungsten_density_at_limiter](name:tungsten_density_at_limiter), which describes tungsten ion density at a limiter, and from tungsten_density_at_plasma_boundary, which applies at the plasma boundary.

items.name: neutral_internal_state_energy_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless closure parameter that limits the admissible energy-flux density carried by neutral particles in a specified internal state.
items.documentation: This coefficient specifies the strength of the limiter applied to energy transport by neutral particles occupying one selected internal state. It is a closure parameter rather than an energy flux or an energy density. The limiter imposes the bound $$ \lvert \mathbf{q}_E \rvert \leq \alpha_E q_{E,\max} $$ where $\alpha_E$ is this flux-limiter coefficient, $\mathbf{q}_E$ is the energy-flux-density vector carried by the selected neutral internal state, and $q_{E,\max}$ is the prescribed maximum admissible magnitude for that energy flux. The coefficient applies to the energy channel of neutral transport for the specified internal state. It does not sum over neutral internal states or neutral species, does not represent the energy flux itself, and has no edge-region restriction in its definition. It is distinct from the corresponding momentum limiter, such as the [neutral internal-state momentum flux-limiter coefficient](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_flux_limiter_coefficient_over_edge_region), which constrains momentum rather than energy transport. The coefficient scales the admissible energy-flux bound in the closure: increasing $\alpha_E$ permits a larger maximum energy flux relative to $q_{E,\max}$, while the coefficient itself remains a dimensionless scalar.

items.name: toroidal_co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Signed toroidal collisional torque per unit volume delivered to a specified bulk thermal-ion species by co-passing fast particles.
items.documentation: Toroidal co-passing thermal-ion collisional torque density is the local toroidal component of the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume delivered to a specified bulk thermal-ion species through Coulomb collisions with co-passing fast particles. Its relation to the vector parent is $$ \tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}} = \boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\tau_{i\phi,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the signed toroidal torque-density component, $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{i,\mathrm{co,coll}}$ is the [co-passing thermal-ion torque-density vector due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions), and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle. The right-handed cylindrical frame is $(R,\phi,Z)$, where $R$ is distance from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The subscripts $i$, $\mathrm{co}$, and $\mathrm{coll}$ identify the receiving ion species, co-passing contribution, and collisional mechanism, respectively. The co-passing restriction applies to the colliding fast-particle distribution, not to the orbit class of the receiving thermal ions. Counter-passing and trapped contributions are excluded. The quantity is local, without spatial averaging or volume integration. Ionic charge-state contributions are summed within the selected species, while different receiving ion species remain distinct; [co-passing thermal-ion charge-state torque density due to collisions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions) retains charge-state resolution in the corresponding vector quantity. This is a population- and component-resolved contribution to [torque density](name:torque_density). The adjacent [toroidal co-passing thermal-electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_co_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) describes transfer to thermal electrons instead and is not included here. Sign convention: Positive when the torque-density component delivered to thermal ions points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: z_first_measurement_direction_unit_vector_of_strain_gauge
items.description: Signed z-axis component of the unit vector along a strain gage's first measurement direction in the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame, with z vertical.
items.documentation: Signed z-axis component of the unit vector along a strain gage's first measurement direction is the scalar direction cosine of that strain-sensitive direction with the vertical basis direction of the right-handed Cartesian frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$. It represents the vertical part of the orientation of the gage's first defined measurement direction. The component is defined by the scalar projection of the first measurement-direction unit vector: $$ u_z^{(1)} = \mathbf{u}^{(1)} \cdot \hat{z} $$ where $\mathbf{u}^{(1)}$ is the unit vector along the strain gage's first measurement direction, $\hat{z}$ is the vertical basis vector of the right-handed Cartesian frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$, and $u_z^{(1)}$ is the signed z-axis component of that unit vector. The scope is one strain gage and its first defined measurement direction; no averaging, summation, or aggregation over gages or measurement directions is implied. This quantity is a direction component, not a position coordinate, displacement, or strain value, and it is distinct from the corresponding component of the second measurement direction. Together with the x-axis component $u_x^{(1)}$ and y-axis component $u_y^{(1)}$, it specifies the orientation of the first measurement direction; because $\mathbf{u}^{(1)}$ is a unit vector, $(u_x^{(1)})^2 + (u_y^{(1)})^2 + (u_z^{(1)})^2 = 1$. Sign convention: Positive when the first measurement-direction unit vector has a component in the $+\hat{z}$ direction of the right-handed Cartesian frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$.

items.name: particle_diffusivity
items.description: Effective Fickian transport coefficient relating particle flux to particle-number-density gradients, with directional or population-specific components represented by more specific quantities.
items.documentation: Particle diffusivity is an effective Fickian coefficient describing the diffusive part of particle transport driven by a particle-number-density gradient. It may be resolved by transport direction or by the particle population being transported. For each resolved direction $i$, the diffusive particle flux is defined by $$ \Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{p,i}\,\frac{\partial n_p}{\partial x_i} $$ where $\Gamma_{p,i}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive particle flux, $D_{p,i}$ is the corresponding diffusivity component, $n_p$ is the particle number density, and $x_i$ is the coordinate along the resolved transport direction. The minus sign defines down-gradient diffusive transport for a positive coefficient. This parent quantity does not specify a particle population, charge-state aggregation, transport direction, or microscopic mechanism. Population- and direction-specific instances include [neutral particle diffusivity](name:neutral_particle_diffusivity) and poloidal particle diffusivity.

items.name: neutron_response_function_of_neutron_detector
items.description: Green-function coefficient giving expected neutron-detector counts from one neutron emitted in a specified plasma voxel and energy bin.
items.documentation: The neutron-detector response function is the expected registered count contribution from a neutron emitted in a specified plasma voxel and neutron-energy bin. It characterizes the detector-specific mapping from neutron emission to detected events. The response enters the forward relation $$ N_d = \sum_v \sum_k G_d(v,E_k)\,S(v,E_k) $$ where $N_d$ is the total expected count for detector $d$, $G_d(v,E_k)$ is this response function, $v$ labels a plasma voxel, $E_k$ labels the $k$th neutron-energy bin, and $S(v,E_k)$ is the neutron yield from voxel $v$ in that bin. The quantity applies to one neutron detector and to the contribution of a specified source voxel and energy bin; its count response is aggregated over the detector events attributable to that source contribution. It is not the neutron emissivity, the geometric acceptance alone, or an energy-dependent efficiency alone. The geometric distinction is given by [solid angle of a neutron detector](name:solid_angle_of_neutron_detector), while [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector) illustrates an efficiency quantity that does not represent this neutron-specific source-to-count response.

items.name: toroidal_magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description: Toroidal magnetic flux change through a poloidal cross-section caused by the pressure-gradient-driven plasma response relative to a reference field without that response.
items.documentation: Toroidal magnetic flux due to diamagnetic drift is the signed, surface-integrated magnetic response associated with pressure-gradient-driven plasma diamagnetism. It is the toroidal specialization of the [magnetic-flux contribution due to diamagnetic drift](name:magnetic_flux_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), defined relative to a corresponding reference field without that response. The contribution through an oriented poloidal cross-section is defined by $$ \Phi_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}} = \int_S \left(\mathbf{B}-\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ref}}\right)\cdot\hat{\phi}\,\mathrm{d}S $$ where $\Phi_{\phi,\mathrm{dia}}$ is the toroidal diamagnetic flux, $S$ is the poloidal integration surface, $\mathbf{B}$ is the equilibrium magnetic field, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the corresponding reference magnetic field with the same external excitation but without the diamagnetic response, and $\mathrm{d}S$ is a positive surface-area element. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector toward increasing toroidal angle; the surface normal is chosen along $\hat{\phi}$. This is a global flux contribution over the specified cross-section, not a local magnetic-field value or a flux value at a particular magnetic surface. It excludes the reference-field flux and is distinct from both total toroidal magnetic flux and poloidal magnetic flux. The [toroidal current density due to diamagnetic drift](name:toroidal_current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) instead describes a local electric-current contribution, not this integrated magnetic response. Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic magnetic-field change produces net flux in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: temperature_of_coil_conductor
items.description: Thermodynamic temperature of the conductor in an active poloidal-field or central-solenoid coil, used to establish its allowable current limit.
items.documentation: This quantity is the thermodynamic temperature of the conducting material in an individual active poloidal-field coil, including central-solenoid and shaping-coil conductors. It applies to the conductor of one active coil and represents the coil's thermal state, not the temperature of a coolant, surrounding structure, or plasma. It is not an aggregate temperature over multiple coils and is distinct from electrical properties such as the [resistance of a poloidal-field coil](name:resistance_of_poloidal_field_coil). The temperature serves as the independent variable for the coil's temperature-dependent maximum allowable current. It therefore identifies the operating-limit condition associated with the conductor temperature, but is not itself a current, resistance, or operating-limit value.

items.name: parallel_ion_momentum_flux
items.description: Parallel ion momentum flux is the rate per unit area at which the magnetic-field-aligned momentum of an ion species crosses an oriented surface.
items.documentation: Parallel ion momentum flux is the transport rate per unit area of the magnetic-field-aligned component of ion [momentum](name:momentum) across an oriented surface. The parallel label selects the transported momentum component, while the surface normal specifies the direction across which transport is evaluated. The defining projection is: $$ \Gamma_{i,\parallel} = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i = \hat{\mathbf b}\cdot\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i\cdot\hat{\mathbf n} $$ where $\Gamma_{i,\parallel}$ is this parallel momentum flux, $i$ identifies the ion species, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_i$ is its momentum-flux vector through the oriented surface, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i$ is its momentum-flux tensor, and $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is the chosen surface-normal unit vector. The magnetic-field unit vector is $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B/|\mathbf B|$, where $\mathbf B$ is the local magnetic field. For the specified ion species, the flux is summed over all ionic charge states, combining the corresponding [parallel ion charge-state momentum flux](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux) contributions. It includes convective transport, pressure, and viscous or turbulent stresses, rather than only diffusive transport; electron and neutral contributions are excluded. The surface need not be a magnetic flux surface, and its normal need not be parallel to the magnetic field. Summing the species contributions gives the parallel component of the total [ion momentum flux](name:ion_momentum_flux), which aggregates over all ion species and ionic charge states. Sign convention: Positive when the net momentum transported through the surface in its chosen normal direction has a component co-directed with the local magnetic field.

items.name: toroidal_fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions
items.description: Volume-integrated toroidal component of the Coulomb-collisional torque on fast ions in a selected charge state, equal to the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine symmetry axis from background plasma species.
items.documentation: The toroidal scalar component of the volume-integrated torque vector exerted by Coulomb collisions on fast (suprathermal) ions in a single specified charge state. It represents the net angular momentum transfer rate about the machine toroidal symmetry axis from background plasma species to this charge-state-resolved energetic ion population. $$ \tau_\phi = \boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_\mathrm{coll}$ is the charge-state-resolved fast-ion collisional torque vector fast_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions and $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$. This quantity covers only the suprathermal ion population in one charge state; the thermal-ion charge-state analog is [thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), the total charge-state collisional torque summed over all species is [total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions](name:total_ion_charge_state_torque_due_to_collisions), and the fast-ion toroidal torque summed over all charge states is [toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions). Sign convention: Positive when the collisional angular momentum transfer is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: stray_breakdown_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Magnitude of the residual magnetic field at the plasma position during initiation, whose incomplete cancelation can inhibit electron-avalanche breakdown.
items.documentation: This quantity is the total strength of the residual magnetic-field contribution present at the plasma position during plasma initiation. It is derived from the vector quantity [stray breakdown magnetic field](name:stray_breakdown_magnetic_field) by removing directional information. $$ B_{\mathrm{stray}} = \left|\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{stray}}\right| = \sqrt{B_R^2 + B_\phi^2 + B_Z^2} $$ where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{stray}}$ is the residual magnetic-field vector, and $B_R$, $B_\phi$, and $B_Z$ are its components in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. The magnitude includes all spatial components caused by imperfect cancelation of external coil fields. It is distinct from any individual directional component and does not encode field orientation or sign.

items.name: total_trapped_particle_density
items.description: Flux-surface-averaged number density of a selected species on magnetically trapped orbits, including both thermal and nonthermal particles.
items.documentation: Total trapped-particle density is the flux-surface-averaged concentration of a selected species on magnetically trapped guiding-center orbits. These orbits undergo magnetic mirror reflection, reversing their motion parallel to the magnetic field rather than circulating as passing orbits. The flux-surface-averaged density is defined by $$ \langle n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}\rangle = \left\langle \int_{\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})} f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v \right\rangle $$ where $s$ labels the selected species, $n_{s,\mathrm{tr}}$ is its local trapped-particle number density, and $f_s$ is its full thermal-plus-nonthermal velocity distribution. The vectors $\mathbf{x}$ and $\mathbf{v}$ denote position and particle velocity, $\mathcal{V}_{\mathrm{tr}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain corresponding to trapped orbits at that position, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. Angle brackets denote the differential-volume-weighted average over a magnetic flux surface. The total includes both thermal and nonthermal trapped particles of the selected species; it does not sum over different species. Passing particles are excluded. This quantity is a flux-surface average, not a local density or a volume-integrated particle count. It equals the sum of the thermal trapped-particle contribution and the nonthermal contribution represented by [trapped fast-particle density](name:trapped_fast_particle_density), with both contributions averaged over the same magnetic flux surface.

items.name: volume_averaged_ion_charge
items.description: Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population.
items.documentation: Volume-averaged ion charge is the spatial average over the confined plasma volume of the charge number of the dominant ionization state for a specified ion species or lumped-ion population. It is a normalized volume average representing the global mean ionization level of that selected charge state. For ion species $i$, the volume-averaged ion charge is defined by $$ \langle Z_{\mathrm{dom},i} \rangle_V = \frac{1}{V_\Omega}\int_\Omega Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{dom},i}(\mathbf{x})$ is the [ion charge](name:ion_charge) number of the dominant ionization state of species $i$ at position $\mathbf{x}$, $\Omega$ is the confined plasma volume, and $V_\Omega$ is the volume of $\Omega$. The population is one specified ion species; if the species represents a lumped-ion population, the same definition applies to that lumped population. The charge-state convention is dominant-state selection: the quantity is not a charge-state sum and is not the density-weighted mean over all charge states. This quantity differs from [volume-averaged ion charge-state average charge number](name:volume_averaged_ion_charge_state_average_charge_number), which represents the density-weighted mean charge number over all charge states of the ion species. It also differs from [volume-averaged ion density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), which is a particle population density rather than a charge number.

items.name: calibration_reference_magnetic_field_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description: Signed poloidal magnetic-field values forming the linear calibration axis used to characterize a poloidal magnetic-field probe’s nonlinear response.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed poloidal magnetic field assigned to the linear-response reference axis of a poloidal magnetic-field probe. It represents the field value corresponding to the probe signal under an assumed linear field-to-signal relation, rather than the corrected field on a nonlinear response curve. The linear calibration relation is represented by $$ S_{\mathrm{lin}} = G B_{\mathrm{ref}} $$ where $S_{\mathrm{lin}}$ is the probe signal predicted by the linear-response model, $G$ is the linear field-to-signal coefficient, and $B_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the signed calibration-reference magnetic field represented by this quantity. The quantity applies to the local poloidal magnetic field at the sensing location of the specified poloidal magnetic-field probe. It retains the signed poloidal field rather than a field magnitude, and no summation over probe locations or magnetic-field components is implied. It is an independent calibration-axis quantity, not a plasma-wide or equilibrium-field aggregate. It is distinct from the local operational field represented by [poloidal magnetic field of a magnetic-field probe](name:poloidal_magnetic_field_of_magnetic_field_probe), which is the probe field value itself, and from the equilibrium reference vector [reference magnetic field](name:reference_magnetic_field). The reference values are paired with the nonlinear-response characterization and do not constitute a single fixed gain or an uncertainty/error quantity. The poloidal component is resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. Sign convention: Positive when the signed poloidal field points along the probe's defined positive sensing direction.

items.name: vertical_length_of_divertor_target
items.description: Non-negative vertical span of a divertor target surface, defined by the difference between its maximum and minimum Z coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The vertical extent of a divertor target is the range of vertical positions occupied by its surface, rather than the vertical position of its center. $$ H_Z = Z_{\\max} - Z_{\\min} $$ where $H_Z$ is the vertical span, and $Z_{\\max}$ and $Z_{\\min}$ are respectively the maximum and minimum vertical coordinates over the target surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \\phi, Z)$ frame. Here, $R$ is major radius, $\\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. This extent complements the [radial length of the divertor target](name:radial_length_of_divertor_target) and is distinct from the [Z coordinate of the divertor target](name:z_coordinate_of_divertor_target), which locates its surface center.

items.name: normalized_effective_particle_energy
items.description: Normalized effective particle energy is the ratio of a species effective particle-energy coordinate to the positive species reference thermal-energy scale.
items.documentation: Normalized effective particle energy is the ratio of a species effective particle-energy coordinate to the positive species reference thermal-energy scale. It is a dimensionless velocity-space coordinate for the effective single-particle energy relative to that species reference, not an independent temperature, mass, or charge ratio. The normalization is $$ \bar{\mathcal{E}}_s = \frac{\mathcal{E}^{*}_{\mathrm{eff},s}}{E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}} $$ where $\bar{\mathcal{E}}_s$ is the normalized effective particle energy, $s$ labels the particle species, $\mathcal{E}^{*}_{\mathrm{eff},s}$ is the effective particle-energy coordinate for that species expressed on a scale compatible with the denominator, and $E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s} > 0$ is the species reference thermal-energy scale. If the reference is specified by a species reference temperature $T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$, the corresponding denominator is $E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}=k_B T_{\mathrm{ref},s}$; the same reference temperature appears in [ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_reference_particle_temperature](name:ratio_of_particle_temperature_to_particle_reference_temperature). It is distinguished from [effective_particle_energy](name:effective_particle_energy), which denotes the effective-energy coordinate without requiring this particular species thermal normalization. If the effective particle energy contains an additive effective-potential term $U_{\mathrm{eff},s}$, its normalized contribution is $U_{\mathrm{eff},s}/E_{\mathrm{th,ref},s}$; with the same denominator this is normalized_particle_effective_potential. The detailed split of the effective energy into kinetic and potential terms and the choice of potential-energy zero are not fixed by this name.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_velocity
items.description: Major-radius projection of the mean flow of ions of one specified species and ionization charge state, directed toward or away from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation: The radial ion charge-state velocity is the projection of the bulk [ion charge-state velocity](name:ion_charge_state_velocity) onto the direction of increasing major radius in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes mean translational motion within one specified ion species and ionization charge state. The component is defined by the projected first velocity moment: $$ u_{R,q}(\mathbf r)=\hat{\mathbf R}\cdot\mathbf u_q(\mathbf r)=\frac{\int (\mathbf v\cdot\hat{\mathbf R})f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\int f_q(\mathbf r,\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{R,q}$ is the radial bulk velocity, $\mathbf u_q$ is the charge-state bulk velocity vector, $q$ is the ionic charge number, $\mathbf r$ is position, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, and $f_q$ is the velocity distribution of the selected species and charge state. The integration covers particle velocity space. Here $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical position, and $\hat{\mathbf R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing $R$. The component is evaluated at the position of maximum major radius on each magnetic flux surface; it is not a flux-surface average. It retains charge-state resolution rather than combining charge states. The corresponding [radial ion velocity](name:radial_ion_velocity) is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of the species, not their sum. This signed component is distinct from flow speed, random thermal motion, and particle flux. The major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface, so this quantity is not a flux-surface-normal velocity. Sign convention: Positive when the charge-state bulk flow projects toward increasing major radius, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all charge states.
items.documentation: Number density of helium-4 ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the helium-4 ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It represents the charge-state-summed helium-4 ion population at that locus. The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_q\int f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He}}$ is the helium-4 ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $q$ is the ionic charge-state index, $f_{{}^{4}\mathrm{He},q}$ is the velocity distribution function of helium-4 ions in charge state $q$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. The plasma boundary is the last closed magnetic flux surface, also called the separatrix, separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. This quantity applies only to helium-4 ions, is evaluated locally at the boundary, includes all helium-4 ionic charge states, and excludes neutral helium-4 atoms. As a species-specific instance of [particle number density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary), it fixes the otherwise unspecified population to helium-4 ions. It differs from flux-surface-averaged helium-4 density at the plasma boundary, which averages the same charge-state-summed population over the boundary surface, and from [helium-3 density at the plasma boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary), which selects a different helium isotope.

items.name: radial_ion_momentum_flux_over_edge_region
items.description: Radial ion momentum flux in the edge region is the signed transfer of a specified ion species' major-radius-directed momentum per unit area and time across a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Radial ion momentum flux in the edge region describes transport of the major-radius component of [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species across a magnetic flux surface. It includes the total momentum transport, rather than an isolated diffusive or convective contribution. The defining projection is: $$ \Gamma_{i,R} = \hat{R} \cdot \boldsymbol{\Pi}_i \cdot \hat{n}_{\mathrm{out}} $$ where $\Gamma_{i,R}$ is this momentum flux, $i$ identifies the ion species, $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_i$ is its total linear-momentum-flux tensor, $\hat{R}$ is the unit vector toward increasing major radius, and $\hat{n}_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface. The major-radius direction belongs to the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The transported momentum projection and the surface-normal transport direction are distinct; the surface normal need not coincide with $\hat{R}$. The flux is summed over all ionic charge states of the specified species, excluding neutral atoms, electrons, and other ion species. Its individual charge-state contributions are [radial ion charge-state momentum fluxes](name:radial_ion_charge_state_momentum_flux). The total tensor includes convective momentum transport, pressure, and viscous or turbulent stresses. This quantity is a flux per unit surface area, not momentum density, a local momentum source, or an area-integrated momentum transfer rate. Sign convention: Positive when the net transport carries momentum directed toward increasing major radius outward across the magnetic flux surface, or equivalently carries momentum directed toward decreasing major radius inward.

items.name: radius_of_reflector
