items.description: Geometric distance from the center of a reflector’s circular aperture to its circumferential boundary in an X-ray crystal spectrometer.
items.documentation: The reflector aperture radius is the geometric distance from the center of the circular opening to its circumferential boundary. It defines the circular cross-section of the optical reflector through which light is directed toward the crystal. For a circular aperture, its area is related to the radius by $$ A = \pi r^2 $$ where $A$ is the aperture area, $r$ is the reflector aperture radius, and $\pi$ is the mathematical constant relating a circle’s circumference to its diameter. This quantity applies only to a reflector with circular aperture geometry. It describes the aperture radius, not a curvature radius of the reflector surface or the radius of a different optical element. The same geometric concept is used for the circular Bragg-crystal opening represented by [radius of Bragg crystal](name:radius_of_bragg_crystal), while [radius of aperture](name:radius_of_aperture) describes a channel-level collimating aperture rather than the reflector aperture.

items.name: nitrogen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description: Number density of nitrogen ions evaluated at the radial position of the internal transport barrier, where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport sustains steep impurity density gradients within the confined plasma.
items.documentation: Nitrogen (atomic number $Z = 7$) is a medium-Z impurity that is seeded into fusion plasmas for radiative power exhaust control and divertor heat-load mitigation. This quantity gives the local number of nitrogen particles per unit volume at the radial reference position of an internal transport barrier (ITB) — a narrow region within the confined plasma where cross-field turbulent transport is locally suppressed, enabling steep radial gradients to develop and persist. Unless a charge-state-resolved quantity is specified separately, it represents the nitrogen ion density summed over all ionization states, consistent with the parent [density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier). In hot plasma core conditions above approximately 1 keV, nitrogen is found predominantly in high ionization states ($N^{5+}$–$N^{7+}$). Within an ITB, neoclassical impurity transport — including temperature-screening and centrifugal effects on the impurity density profile — can drive strong inward or outward peaking of $n_\mathrm{N}$ at the barrier radius, with direct consequences for the local $Z_\mathrm{eff}$ and radiated power balance. Nitrogen density in the plasma core is measured by charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, which resolves individual charge states whose sum yields the total impurity density; transport analysis then extracts the value at the ITB reference location from the fitted profile. Compare with [neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:neon_density_at_internal_transport_barrier) for a noble-gas impurity of similar use, and with [nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:nitrogen_density_at_plasma_boundary) for the corresponding boundary value of the same species.

items.name: volumetric_fraction_of_breeder_blanket_layer
items.description: Volumetric fraction of a breeder blanket layer is the share of a specified constituent material or phase in the layer's bulk volume. It is a dimensionless effective-medium composition parameter for homogenized breeder-blanket layer properties.
items.documentation: Volumetric fraction of a breeder blanket layer is the part-to-whole volume ratio for one specified constituent material, phase, void region, coolant region, or gas region within a breeder blanket layer. It describes the layer composition used for homogenized material properties over the same geometric region. For constituent $i$, the fraction is defined by: $$ f_i = \frac{V_i}{V_\mathrm{layer}} $$ where $f_i$ is the volumetric fraction, $V_i$ is the volume of constituent $i$ in cubic meters, and $V_\mathrm{layer}$ is the total bulk volume of the same breeder blanket layer in cubic meters over the homogenization region. The numerator and denominator must refer to the same layer region. For an exhaustive non-overlapping partition of that region, $0 \le f_i \le 1$ and $\sum_i f_i = 1$; separately represented voids, coolant, or gas regions are included as their own constituents. This quantity is distinct from mass fraction, atomic fraction, porosity, and selected-solid packing factor, and its layer denominator differs from the whole-blanket volume described by volume of breeder blanket.

items.name: electron_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient
items.description: Dimensionless multiplier that limits electron particle-flux density relative to its collisionless free-streaming bound without reversing the transport direction.
items.documentation: The electron particle flux limiter coefficient is a multiplicative factor that scales the collisionless free-streaming upper bound on electron particle-flux density in a particle-transport closure. It limits the permitted magnitude while preserving the direction or sign assigned by the underlying closure. The admissible electron particle-flux magnitude satisfies: $$ \left\lVert\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e\right\rVert \leq \Gamma_{e,\max} = L_e\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}} $$ where $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is the electron particle-flux density, the norm denotes its magnitude, $\Gamma_{e,\max}$ is its maximum permitted magnitude, $L_e$ is the electron particle flux limiter coefficient, and $\Gamma_e^{\mathrm{fs}}$ is the nonnegative collisionless free-streaming bound. The subscript $e$ denotes electrons. The coefficient is nonnegative; values below unity impose a stricter cap than the free-streaming bound. This bound does not prescribe a particular interpolation between unconstrained and limited transport. This coefficient applies to the electron density equation, not to electron energy or momentum transport. It is the electron-specific specialization of the [particle flux limiter coefficient](name:particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), within the broader [flux limiter coefficient](name:flux_limiter_coefficient) family. It is distinct from the [ion particle flux limiter coefficient](name:ion_particle_flux_limiter_coefficient), which limits ion particle transport.

items.name: line_averaged_argon_density
items.description: Chord-averaged number density of argon ions along a specified plasma path, with contributions from all ionization stages summed together.
items.documentation: Line-averaged argon ion number density is the argon ion concentration averaged along a specified chord through the plasma, including all ionization stages. The line average is defined by $$ \overline{n}_\mathrm{Ar} = \frac{1}{L} \int_0^L \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}(\mathbf{r}(l))\,dl $$ where $L$ is the chord length, $l$ is distance along the chord, $\mathbf{r}(l)$ is the position on the chord, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar},q}$ is the local number density of argon ions in charge state $q$. This path average is distinct from the local [argon ion density](name:argon_density) and from the plasma-volume average [volume-averaged argon density](name:volume_averaged_argon_density).

items.name: molecular_neutral_species_flow_at_outlet
items.description: Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is defined by the outlet partial pressure of that species and the corresponding effective pumping speed, not by total neutral pressure.
items.documentation: Molecular neutral species flow at an outlet is the pressure-volume throughput of one molecular neutral species removed across a pumping outlet. It is species-specific and uses the outlet partial pressure of that molecular neutral species rather than the [total neutral pressure](name:total_neutral_pressure). The outlet throughput is defined by the product of the outlet species partial pressure and the effective pumping speed for that species: $$ Q_{s,\mathrm{out}} = p_{s,\mathrm{out}} S_{s,\mathrm{out}} $$ where $Q_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is this molecular neutral species flow at the outlet, $p_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the outlet partial pressure of molecular neutral species $s$, and $S_{s,\mathrm{out}}$ is the effective pumping speed for species $s$ at the outlet. This quantity is an outlet removal throughput, distinct from a gas source into the vessel such as [gas injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection). It is the molecular, species-resolved outlet form of neutral species flow and a species-specific specialization of gas flow. Sign convention: Positive when the molecular neutral species is removed through the outlet in the pumping direction away from the vessel.

items.name: surface_area_of_flux_surface
items.description: Surface area of a complete magnetic flux surface, including its full poloidal and toroidal extent rather than the enclosed poloidal cross-section.
items.documentation: Area of flux surface The area is defined by $$ A = \iint_{\mathcal S} dS $$ where $A$ is the surface area, $\mathcal S$ is the specified flux surface, and $dS$ is the nonnegative geometric surface-area element. This quantity applies to one complete flux surface, not solely to the plasma boundary. It is integrated over the entire surface and is neither a local area element nor a flux-surface average. Unlike the [poloidal-plane cross-sectional area](name:poloidal_plane_cross_sectional_area_of_flux_surface), it measures the surface itself rather than the planar region enclosed by its contour. It also differs from the [enclosed volume](name:volume_of_flux_surface), which measures the full interior bounded by the same surface. A surface formed by points sharing the same magnetic-flux label in a nested-flux-surface configuration. Where $\psi(R, Z) = \mathrm{const}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux.

items.name: radius_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description: Radius of the circular ion-source surface from which neutral beams are extracted, defining the radial extent of its extraction aperture.
items.documentation: This quantity is the radius of the circular ion-source surface from which a neutral-beam injector extracts its beam. It defines the radial extent of the extraction aperture. For a circular boundary, the radius is the distance from the surface center to any point on its circumference: $$ r_s = \left\lVert \mathbf{x}-\mathbf{x}_c \right\rVert $$ where $r_s$ is the ion-source-surface radius, $\mathbf{x}$ is the position of a point on the circular boundary, $\mathbf{x}_c$ is the position of the circle center, and the norm denotes Euclidean distance. The quantity applies to one neutral-beam injector unit and only to its circular ion-source geometry. It is not an aggregate over injector units and does not represent the radius of a beamlet-group tangency surface or another injector-associated aperture. For a rectangular ion-source aperture, the corresponding transverse dimensions are given by the [first local tangential width of the neutral-beam injector](name:first_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector) and [second local tangential width of the neutral-beam injector](name:second_local_tangential_width_of_neutral_beam_injector), rather than by this radius.

items.name: height_of_plasma_filament
items.description: Full vertical extent of the rectangular cross-section of a discrete plasma current-carrying filament element, measured along the machine’s vertical axis.
items.documentation: This quantity is the full vertical dimension of the rectangular cross-section associated with one discrete plasma current-carrying filament. It is a geometric extent, not the filament current or its current density. The height $H$ is defined by the difference between the upper and lower vertical coordinates: $$ H = Z_{\mathrm{upper}} - Z_{\mathrm{lower}} $$ where $Z_{\mathrm{upper}}$ and $Z_{\mathrm{lower}}$ are the upper and lower coordinates in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with $Z$ denoting vertical height and $\hat{Z}$ the vertical basis direction. This quantity applies only to the vertical dimension of the rectangular filament cross-section. The horizontal full width is defined separately by [plasma filament width](name:plasma_filament_width), while the in-plane thickness is defined by thickness of plasma filament.

items.name: area_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting cross section of one poloidal-field-coil element in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle φ of the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation: Non-negative full geometric area of the conducting cross section of one poloidal-field-coil element is the surface measure of the conductor region enclosed by that element boundary. It is defined in a poloidal plane at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For an arbitrary conductor cross-section, the area is the integral of the differential surface measure over the conductor region $\mathcal{S}$: $$ A = \int_{\mathcal{S}} dS $$ where $A$ is the area of the poloidal-field-coil element, $\mathcal{S}$ is the conductor region in the poloidal plane, and $dS$ is the differential surface measure on that plane. The quantity is per coil element, not a sum over multiple elements or over a complete coil. For a rectangular cross-section aligned with the $R$ and $Z$ directions of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $A = W H$, where $W$ is [width_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:width_of_poloidal_field_coil) and $H$ is [height_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:height_of_poloidal_field_coil); [thickness_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:thickness_of_poloidal_field_coil) is a separate geometric extent and is not the radial width in this relationship. For an annular cross-section, $A = \pi(r_\mathrm{out}^2-r_\mathrm{in}^2)$, where $r_\mathrm{out}$ is [outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) and $r_\mathrm{in}$ is [inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil](name:inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil). An insulation envelope, winding-pack envelope, or effective conducting area is a distinct quantity unless it is defined by the same boundary as $\mathcal{S}$.

items.name: lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description: Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary, evaluated locally on the last closed magnetic flux surface and summed over all ionization states.
items.documentation: Number density of lithium ions at the plasma boundary is the local particle count per physical volume for the lithium-ion population evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface. The plasma boundary is the separatrix separating confined plasma from the open-field-line scrape-off layer. The defining charge-state-summed zeroth velocity-space moment is $$ n_{\mathrm{Li}}(\mathbf{x}_b,t)=\sum_{Z=1}^{3}\int f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}(\mathbf{x}_b,\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3\mathbf{v} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the lithium-ion number density, $\mathbf{x}_b$ is a point on the plasma boundary, $t$ is time, $Z$ is the lithium ionization-state index, $f_{\mathrm{Li}^{Z+}}$ is the velocity distribution function for lithium ions in charge state $Z+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, and $d^3\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space volume element. This quantity is local at the plasma boundary and is not averaged over the boundary flux surface. It includes lithium ions from Li+ through Li3+, summed over these charge states, and excludes neutral lithium. It is the lithium-specific specialization of [density at the plasma boundary](name:density_at_plasma_boundary). The corresponding flux-surface-averaged quantity, flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary, applies a flux-surface average to the same charge-state-summed lithium-ion density. The boundary locus also distinguishes this quantity from [lithium density at the limiter](name:lithium_density_at_limiter), which is evaluated at a limiter rather than at the plasma boundary.

items.name: trapped_fast_particle_pressure
items.description: Scalar trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by the total suprathermal population on magnetically trapped orbits. It combines field-aligned and transverse stress contributions and may be evaluated locally or averaged over a magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation: Trapped fast-particle pressure is one-third of the kinetic-stress trace carried by suprathermal particles on magnetically trapped orbits. It is the trapped-orbit contribution to [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure); taking the scalar trace does not require the field-aligned and transverse stresses to be equal. At position $\mathbf{x}$, the local pressure is defined by the trapped-particle second velocity moment: $$ p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{3}\sum_s\sum_c m_s \int_{\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})} |\mathbf{v}|^2 f_{s,c}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}$ is the trapped fast-particle pressure, $\mathbf{x}$ is spatial position, $s$ labels a fast-particle species, $c$ labels its charge state, $m_s$ is the mass of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $|\mathbf{v}|$ is particle speed, $f_{s,c}$ is the distribution function for suprathermal particles of species $s$ and charge state $c$, $\mathcal{T}_{s,c}(\mathbf{x})$ is the velocity-space domain of those particles on magnetically trapped orbits at $\mathbf{x}$, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space integration element. The quantity applies to the total suprathermal population: contributions are added over fast-particle species and summed over all charge states, not density-weighted across charge states. It excludes thermal particles and fast particles on co-passing or counter-passing orbits. The local value retains spatial variation; flux-surface averaging gives an average over the surface and is not part of the trapped-orbit selection itself. The [parallel trapped fast-particle pressure](name:parallel_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the field-aligned stress component, and the [perpendicular trapped fast-particle pressure](name:perpendicular_trapped_fast_particle_pressure), $p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}}$, is the mean stress per transverse degree of freedom for the same population. Their relation to the scalar trace is $p_{\mathrm{tr,f}}=(p_{\parallel,\mathrm{tr,f}}+2p_{\perp,\mathrm{tr,f}})/3$. For a common population and spatial aggregation, the trapped contribution together with [co-passing fast-particle pressure](name:co_passing_fast_particle_pressure) and [counter-passing fast-particle pressure](name:counter_passing_fast_particle_pressure) sums to the [fast-particle pressure](name:fast_particle_pressure) when those orbit classes partition the population.

items.name: vertical_volumetric_force
items.description: Vertical component of the electromagnetic body-force density vector acting on plasma volumes or conducting wall and structural elements, projected onto increasing vertical height Z in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The vertical volumetric force is the $\hat{Z}$-projection of the local electromagnetic body-force density vector acting on plasma volumes or conducting wall and structural elements. It characterizes the local mechanical load per unit volume along the vertical coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, and $\hat{Z}$ is the positive vertical basis direction. The component is defined by projecting the local Lorentz force density onto $\hat{Z}$: $$ f_Z = (\mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B}) \cdot \hat{Z} $$ where $f_Z$ is the vertical volumetric force, $\mathbf{J}$ is current density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is magnetic field. The quantity is local to the plasma, conducting wall, or structural material at the point where the force density is defined; no spatial or component aggregation is implied. It is distinct from a coordinate value, a surface traction, a pressure, the magnitude of the force-density vector, and the net vertical force obtained by integrating over a material volume. Together with the [radial volumetric force](name:radial_volumetric_force) and [toroidal volumetric force](name:toroidal_volumetric_force), it forms the component decomposition of the [volumetric force](name:volumetric_force) in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. Sign convention: Positive when the force component points in the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: toroidal_ion_momentum_damping_rate
items.description: Effective inverse relaxation time for dissipative decay of the toroidal bulk-flow momentum of a specified ion species, aggregated over its ionic charge states.
items.documentation: The toroidal ion momentum damping rate quantifies dissipative relaxation of ordered toroidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion species on magnetic flux surfaces. The toroidal direction follows increasing toroidal angle in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. In a linear flow-damping closure, the damping contribution to the momentum balance is: $$ \left.\frac{\partial p_{i,\phi}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{damp}} = -\nu_{i,\phi}p_{i,\phi} $$ where $\nu_{i,\phi}$ is this damping rate, $p_{i,\phi}$ is the toroidal bulk-flow momentum density summed over the species' ionic charge states, $t$ is time, and the index $i$ identifies the ion species. The restricted derivative includes only the damping contribution. A constant positive rate produces exponential decay under this term alone. The coefficient applies to one ion species, not to the combined momentum of all plasma species. Its underlying bulk velocity is the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states, excluding neutral particles; the rate is an effective coefficient for that aggregate flow, not a sum of charge-state damping rates. The [toroidal ion charge-state momentum damping rate](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_damping_rate) instead applies to a specified charge state. This quantity is the toroidal flow-component coefficient of the [ion momentum damping rate](name:ion_momentum_damping_rate). It describes relaxation rather than diffusive or convective transport of momentum between flux surfaces, and it excludes imposed momentum sources. The effective damping may include collisional, neoclassical, or anomalous contributions; no single mechanism is prescribed.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Effective Fickian coefficient relating major-radius-directed diffusive particle flux to the opposing number-density gradient for ions of one species and charge state.
items.documentation: The radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient characterizes particle diffusion of one specified ion species and charge state along the major-radius direction. It selects the radial-radial diagonal response in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For the diffusive flux contribution driven by the major-radius density gradient, the defining relation is: $$ \Gamma_{s,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff},RR} = -D_{s,q,RR}\frac{\partial n_{s,q}}{\partial R} $$ where $s$ identifies the ion species, $q$ is its ionic charge number, $\Gamma_{s,q,R}^{\mathrm{diff},RR}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux density contributed by this diagonal response, $D_{s,q,RR}$ is the radial ion charge-state diffusion coefficient, and $n_{s,q}$ is that species' number density in the specified charge state. The derivative is taken at fixed toroidal angle and vertical height. The minus sign expresses down-gradient transport for positive diffusivity. The population includes thermal and nonthermal ions of the specified species and charge state, without summing over charge states. This is a particle transport coefficient, not an energy or momentum transport coefficient, and it excludes convective contributions. The major-radius direction is not generally normal to magnetic flux surfaces or perpendicular to the magnetic field. This is the radial-radial diagonal specialization of the [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient), not a sum of directional coefficients. Off-diagonal diffusion-tensor couplings, when present, provide additional radial flux contributions outside the defining relation above. In contrast, the [ion diffusion coefficient](name:ion_diffusion_coefficient) applies to a charge-state-summed ion population; its effective value is not obtained by simply summing charge-state diffusion coefficients.

items.name: ion_charge_state_diffusivity
items.description: Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection.
items.documentation:
Ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state, without specifying a spatial projection. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the diffusive particle flux component of that charge state to the negative directional gradient of its number density. For a chosen projection direction $\hat{\mathbf{e}}$, the defining Fickian relation is: $$ \Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e} = -D_s\,
abla_e n_s $$ where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,e}$ is the projected diffusive particle flux density of charge state $s$, $D_s$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the number density of charge state $s$, and $
abla_e n_s = \hat{\mathbf{e}}\cdot
abla n_s$ is the directional derivative of that number density. A positive flux component is directed along $+\hat{\mathbf{e}}$; the minus sign makes a positive diffusivity drive diffusive flux opposite to the projected density gradient. This quantity is charge-state-resolved: it applies to a single ionization state rather than to the density-weighted mean over all charge states represented by ion diffusivity. It is the same physical coefficient as [ion charge-state diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when that name is used for the same Fickian closure. Directionally specified counterparts include [radial ion charge-state diffusivity](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and [parallel ion charge-state diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_diffusivity); convective or pinch transport, particle sources and sinks, and energy or momentum transport coefficients are separate quantities.

items.name: wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna
items.description: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna specifies the relative angular offset of coherent radio-frequency excitations at selected straps or modules.
items.documentation: Wave phase at an ion-cyclotron heating antenna is the relative phase of a coherent radio-frequency excitation associated with a selected strap or module. It describes excitation phasing rather than an absolute phase independent of a reference. For selected and reference excitations, the relative phase is defined by $$ \varphi = \arg\!\left(A_{\mathrm{sel}} A_{\mathrm{ref}}^*\right) \pmod{2\pi} $$ where $\varphi$ is the wave phase, $A_{\mathrm{sel}}$ is the selected complex excitation phasor, $A_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is the coherent reference excitation phasor, the superscript $*$ denotes complex conjugation, and $\arg$ extracts the complex argument. Both phasors must be nonzero and refer to the same radio-frequency component. The phase is defined modulo $2\pi$. The scope includes relative phasing between antenna straps or modules, without summation or averaging over elements. The excitation quantity, reference excitation, reference planes, and temporal phasor convention must be specified. Feed-voltage phase and traveling power-wave phase are distinct realizations and are not interchangeable without their electrical relationship. Relative element phasing affects interference between excitations and therefore the launched wave spectrum and current-drive efficiency. The [forward-wave phase](name:forward_wave_phase_of_ion_cyclotron_heating_antenna) specializes this quantity to forward power-wave phasors referenced to the first module; that reference is not imposed on the general quantity. The [wave phase of an antenna strap](name:wave_phase_of_antenna_strap) specifically identifies the phase of its radio-frequency current phasor. Neither phase quantity includes excitation magnitude. Sign convention: Positive when the selected excitation phasor leads the reference excitation phasor in phase under the declared temporal phasor convention.

items.name: nuclear_power_density_of_breeder_blanket_layer
items.description: Local rate of nuclear energy deposition within the material volume of one breeder blanket layer, generated by neutron interactions and associated photon absorption.
items.documentation: Nuclear power density is the local volumetric heat-generation rate within one defined breeder blanket material layer. It includes energy deposited by neutron interactions and by absorption of primary or secondary photons, rather than surface heat loads or externally applied heating. The volume integral gives the corresponding layer-integrated nuclear heating power: $$ P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{layer}}} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V $$ where $q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local nuclear power density, $P_{\mathrm{nuc,layer}}$ is the integrated nuclear heating power, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $V_{\mathrm{layer}}$ is the material volume of the layer. This quantity is the nuclear-deposition component of power density of a breeder blanket layer and integrates to [nuclear heating power of a breeder blanket layer](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_breeder_blanket_layer).

items.name: argon_density_at_separatrix
items.description: Charge-state-summed number density of argon ions, excluding neutral argon, evaluated locally on the magnetic separatrix.
items.documentation: Argon ion density at the separatrix is the local number of charged argon ions per physical volume on the last closed magnetic flux surface. It is the argon-specific component of density at separatrix. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{Ar}} = \sum_{q=1}^{18} n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon ion number density, $q$ is the argon ion charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{Ar}^{q+}}$ is the number density of argon ions in charge state $q$. Neutral argon is excluded. Unlike flux-surface-averaged argon density at the plasma boundary, this quantity denotes the local value at the separatrix.

items.name: electron_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission
items.description: Kinetic-energy power carried away per unit wall area by electrons emitted from a plasma-facing surface after passage through the sheath.
items.documentation: This quantity is the outward kinetic-energy flux density carried by electrons released from a plasma-facing wall through surface-emission processes. It represents energy transported by the emitted electron population after sheath transmission. The emitted electron kinetic-energy flux density is related to the emitted particle flux and the mean kinetic energy per emitted electron by $$ q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}} = \Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}\,\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}} $$ where $q_{\mathrm{e,kin}}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is this kinetic-energy flux density, $\Gamma_{\mathrm e}^{\mathrm{em}}$ is the [electron particle flux due to surface emission](name:electron_particle_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), and $\overline{E}_{\mathrm{kin,e}}$ is the mean kinetic energy carried by each emitted electron. The quantity applies specifically to emitted electrons at the wall surface and is aggregated over the emitted electron population, rather than representing an individual electron energy or a spatial maximum. It excludes energy carried by incident electrons, emitted ions, emitted photons, and non-kinetic energy of emitted electrons. It is the electron kinetic contribution to the broader [energy flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission), which also includes other emitted energy channels. It is distinct from the incident wall energy represented by energy flux at the wall and from the corresponding emitted-ion quantity [ion kinetic energy flux at the wall due to surface emission](name:ion_kinetic_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_surface_emission). Sign convention: Positive when kinetic energy is carried away from the wall into the plasma.

items.name: radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary coefficient of the radial component of a complex perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction for one toroidal linear-MHD mode in the vacuum region.
items.documentation: This quantity is the imaginary coefficient of the radial component of the complex perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction for a single toroidal linear-MHD mode in the vacuum region. The radial imaginary coefficient is defined by $$ A_{R,\mathrm{imag}} = \operatorname{Im}\left(\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{R}}\right) $$ where $A_{R,\mathrm{imag}}$ is this quantity, $\operatorname{Im}$ extracts the imaginary part, $\widetilde{\mathbf{A}}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the complex perturbed magnetic vector-potential eigenfunction in the vacuum region, and $\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ is the radial unit vector. The radial direction is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The scope is the vacuum region outside the plasma and one specified toroidal Fourier mode; coefficients from different toroidal modes are not summed. This quantity contains only the out-of-phase imaginary coefficient and excludes the corresponding real part. The [parent radial perturbed vacuum magnetic vector potential](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) is the full complex radial component before imaginary-part extraction. It is distinct from the [imaginary radial perturbed vacuum magnetic field](name:radial_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part), because the magnetic-field perturbation is obtained from the curl of the vector potential rather than being the vector-potential component itself. Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary part of the vector-potential coefficient points in the increasing-$R$ radial direction; its phase sign follows the chosen phase reference of the complex eigenfunction.

items.name: vertical_neutral_velocity
items.description: Mean directed motion of a selected neutral species along the vertical symmetry-axis direction, averaged over contributing internal states with number-density weighting.
items.documentation: The vertical neutral velocity is the projection of the bulk drift of a selected neutral species onto the direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents directed motion after averaging over particle velocities and contributing internal states. In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical position, its local definition is: $$ u_{0,Z}=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\mathbf u_0=\hat{\mathbf z}\cdot\frac{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int\mathbf v\,f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v}{\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}\int f_{0,a}(\mathbf v)\,d^3v} $$ where $u_{0,Z}$ is the vertical neutral velocity, $\mathbf u_0$ is the [neutral velocity](name:neutral_velocity) vector, $\hat{\mathbf z}$ is the unit vector along the vertical symmetry axis, $\mathbf v$ is particle velocity, $f_{0,a}$ is the local velocity distribution of neutral internal state $a$, and $\mathcal A$ is the set of contributing internal states. The subscript $0$ denotes neutral particles, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The state distributions combine with number-density weighting for one selected neutral species, not by summing state velocities or averaging different species together. This is a local flow component, including for neutrals in the scrape-off layer and divertor, rather than a spatial average, flow-speed magnitude, particle flux, or random thermal spread. Unlike [bulk neutral internal-state velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity), which retains one specified internal state, this quantity averages over the contributing internal states before taking the vertical projection. Sign convention: Positive when the neutral bulk flow points toward increasing vertical position $Z$.

items.name: lithium_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Local number density of charged lithium ions at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, summed over all lithium ionization states and excluding neutral lithium.
items.documentation: Lithium-ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal is the local concentration of charged lithium particles at the pedestal's inner shoulder, where the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal) identifies the evaluation location. The charge-state-summed density is defined by $$ n_{\mathrm{Li}} = \sum_{q=1}^{3} n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}} $$ where $n_{\mathrm{Li}}$ is the total charged-lithium number density, $q$ is the lithium ionization charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{Li}^{q+}}$ is the number density of lithium ions in charge state $q$. The aggregation includes Li$^+$, Li$^{2+}$, and Li$^{3+}$ and excludes neutral lithium. This quantity is a local value at the pedestal top, not a line average such as [line-averaged lithium density](name:line_averaged_lithium_density) or a flux-surface average such as [flux-surface-averaged lithium density at the plasma boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_lithium_density_at_plasma_boundary). Its species scope is lithium only, and its charge-state aggregation is a sum over all charged lithium ionization states.

items.name: voltage_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe
items.description: Terminal voltage induced at the terminals of a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil by time variation of the local toroidal magnetic-field component in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame threading the coil windings.
items.documentation: Terminal voltage induced at the terminals of a toroidal magnetic-field probe coil is the signed electric potential difference produced by Faraday induction in a coil sensitive to the toroidal magnetic-field component. The toroidal component is $B_\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. For fixed probe geometry, the defining Faraday-law relation is $$ V_\phi(t) = -\frac{d\Lambda_\phi(t)}{dt} $$ where $V_\phi$ is the terminal voltage, $\Lambda_\phi$ is the signed magnetic-flux linkage of the toroidal magnetic-field probe, and $t$ is time. This quantity applies to one toroidal magnetic-field probe coil and to the local region whose magnetic flux threads that coil. It is not an aggregate over multiple probes, and it excludes the integrated or calibrated local toroidal magnetic-field component derived from the raw terminal voltage. For a uniform local-field approximation, $\Lambda_\phi = N_\phi A_\phi B_\phi$, where $N_\phi$ is the signed [turn count of the toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:turn_count_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe) and $A_\phi$ is the effective sensitive area set by the probe geometry, including the [length of the toroidal magnetic-field probe](name:length_of_toroidal_magnetic_field_probe). Relative to a reference time $t_0$, the corresponding calibrated field change satisfies $B_\phi(t)-B_\phi(t_0) = -(N_\phi A_\phi)^{-1}\int_{t_0}^{t} V_\phi(t')\,dt'$ when the same fixed sensitivity applies. The corresponding terminal-voltage quantity for a probe sensitive to the poloidal magnetic-field component is [voltage of poloidal magnetic-field probe](name:voltage_of_poloidal_magnetic_field_probe). Sign convention: Positive when the signed magnetic-flux linkage of the toroidal magnetic-field probe is decreasing in time.

items.name: electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Torque density due to collisional processes is the angular-momentum transfer rate per unit volume imparted to the electron population, encompassing fast and thermal electrons.
items.documentation: Torque density due to collisional processes is the local rate of angular-momentum transfer to the electron population per unit volume. It is the common parent of the fast- and thermal-electron specializations, which distinguish the electron populations receiving the collisional transfer. Using $\dot{L}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}$ for the collisional angular-momentum transfer rate to electrons and $V$ for volume, the torque density is defined by $$ \tau_{e,\mathrm{coll}} = \frac{\partial \dot{L}_{e,\mathrm{coll}}}{\partial V} $$ The quantity refines [torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:torque_density_due_to_collisions), while [fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:fast_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) provide its population-specific forms. The corresponding ion-family quantity is [ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions); this name does not imply a volume-integrated torque. Sign convention: Positive when collisions transfer angular momentum to electrons in the positive direction defined for the torque component.

items.name: turns_per_metre_of_rogowski_coil
items.description: Linear winding density of a Rogowski coil, specifying the number of turns in a single winding layer per unit coil length.
items.documentation: The turns-per-length quantity specifies the linear winding density of a Rogowski coil. For a multilayer winding, it refers to one winding layer rather than the combined count of all layers. The winding density is defined by $$ n_t = \frac{N_\ell}{\ell} $$ where $n_t$ is the Rogowski-coil turns density, $N_\ell$ is the number of complete winding turns in one layer over the selected winding length, and $\ell$ is that winding length. This quantity applies to the physical winding of the Rogowski coil and is a linear density, not a discrete total turn count. It excludes the effective cross-sectional area, which is a separate geometric quantity described by the [area of the Rogowski coil](name:area_of_rogowski_coil), and it does not represent the signed winding current described by the [current of the Rogowski coil](name:current_of_rogowski_coil). The winding density and effective cross-sectional area together determine the coil's electromagnetic coupling and therefore its current-sensing sensitivity.

items.name: radial_derivative_of_poloidal_magnetic_flux
items.description: Rate of change of signed poloidal magnetic flux with the dimensionful toroidal-flux radius labeling nested equilibrium flux surfaces.
items.documentation: The radial derivative of poloidal magnetic flux is the rate at which the signed poloidal magnetic flux changes across nested equilibrium magnetic flux surfaces. It is a metric coefficient relating the poloidal-flux and toroidal-flux coordinate descriptions. The defining relation is $$ \frac{d\psi}{d\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}} $$ where $\psi$ is the [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the dimensionful toroidal-flux radius that labels the nested surfaces. This quantity is evaluated as a function of the toroidal-flux radius, with one derivative value associated with each nested equilibrium surface. It is not a surface integral or average, and it is distinct from a derivative with respect to the cylindrical major radius, minor radius, or a normalized flux coordinate. Relative to [poloidal magnetic flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), this quantity describes how the flux label changes in the outward toroidal-flux-radial direction. It has the same independent coordinate as the derivative with respect to toroidal flux coordinate of area of flux surface, but differentiates poloidal magnetic flux rather than enclosed surface area. Sign convention: Positive when the poloidal magnetic flux increases as $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ increases outward from the magnetic axis toward the plasma boundary.

items.name: neutron_flux_maximum_at_first_wall
items.description: Maximum neutron flux at the first wall of a breeding-blanket module is the largest local neutron energy flux on that module first-wall surface, identifying the highest local neutron loading relevant to material damage and blanket lifetime.
items.documentation: Maximum neutron flux at the first wall of a breeding-blanket module is the largest local neutron energy flux on the module first-wall surface. It represents the peak neutron loading of that surface. The quantity is defined by the surface maximum of the local neutron energy-flux field: $$ q_{n,\mathrm{FW}}^{\max} = \max_{\mathbf{x}\in S_{\mathrm{FW}}^{\mathrm{module}}} q_n(\mathbf{x}) $$ where $q_{n,\mathrm{FW}}^{\max}$ is the maximum neutron flux at the first wall of a breeding-blanket module, $q_n(\mathbf{x})$ is the local neutron energy flux at surface position $\mathbf{x}$, and $S_{\mathrm{FW}}^{\mathrm{module}}$ is the first-wall surface of that breeding-blanket module. The scope is a single breeding-blanket module and only its first-wall surface. The aggregation convention is a spatial maximum over that surface; it is not an area average, a surface integral, or a module total. It excludes neutron flux on the module back surface and on other module surfaces, and it excludes contributions from non-neutron energy carriers. The same local neutron energy-flux field can be evaluated on other surfaces; [maximum of back-surface neutron flux](name:maximum_of_back_surface_neutron_flux) is the corresponding surface maximum on the module back surface. The related [energy-flux maximum at the first wall](name:energy_flux_maximum_at_first_wall) is the maximum of the total local energy-flux field; this neutron maximum is not generally the neutron contribution evaluated at the location of the total maximum, because the positions of the neutron-field maximum and total-field maximum can differ.

items.name: parallel_effective_neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection
items.description: Parallel effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection is the signed, field-aligned component of the effective convection velocity representing transport of momentum carried by neutrals in a resolved internal state. The parallel direction is along the local magnetic field.
items.documentation: Parallel effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection is the scalar component, along the local magnetic-field direction, of an effective convection velocity for transport of momentum carried by a neutral population in one resolved internal state. It is a transport velocity for momentum, not the neutral bulk-flow velocity itself. The scalar projection is defined by $$ v_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}} = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{b}} $$ where $v_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}$ is this parallel effective neutral internal-state momentum velocity due to convection, $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the corresponding [neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection](name:neutral_internal_state_momentum_velocity_due_to_convection), and $\hat{\mathbf{b}} = \mathbf{B}/\lvert\mathbf{B}\rvert$ is the unit vector in the direction of the local magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The scope is a single resolved neutral internal state, so no summation or averaging over internal states is implied. This quantity is the field-aligned component only; it excludes perpendicular components, particle-density convection velocities, energy convection velocities, diffusivities, and source terms. In a convective momentum-transport closure, it is the effective velocity factor associated with the transported neutral internal-state momentum. Sign convention: Positive when the projection of the effective convection velocity is in the direction of the local magnetic field.

items.name: particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description: Particle torque due to j cross B force is the volume-integrated Lorentz-force torque exerted on a represented particle distribution by its electric current density interacting with the magnetic field. It is the particle-distribution-resolved parent quantity; species- or population-specific names refine it without implying a toroidal-only projection.
items.documentation: Particle torque due to j-cross-B force is the volume-integrated torque exerted on a represented particle distribution by the Lorentz force density generated from that distribution's electric current density and the magnetic field. The physical torque is an axial-vector quantity before any species, population, or coordinate-component qualifier is applied. The defining volume integral is $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_p = \int_V \mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}\right)\, dV $$ where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ is the particle-distribution-resolved torque, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the torque origin to the volume element, $\mathbf{j}_p$ is the electric current density carried by the represented particle distribution, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, and $V$ is the integration volume. This parent does not specify fast, thermal, impurity, neutral, or other particle populations and does not by itself select any coordinate-component projection. Population-specific instances, such as [fast-particle torque due to j-cross-B force](name:fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force), inherit this definition; component-specific quantities are projections of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ rather than redefinitions of the torque source. It excludes torque contributions not arising from the Lorentz force density $\mathbf{j}_p \times \mathbf{B}$ and excludes sums over unrelated plasma sources unless the represented particle distribution is explicitly the aggregation being described. Sign convention: Positive when a scalar component of $\boldsymbol{\tau}_p$ is aligned with the positive direction of the explicitly named projection axis; for a toroidal projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, this is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: poloidal_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description: Effective velocity coefficient relating the non-diffusive convective flux of poloidal momentum to the poloidal momentum density of ions of one species in a specified charge state.
items.documentation: This coefficient governs advective, non-diffusive transport of poloidal [momentum](name:momentum) carried by ions of one specified species and charge state. It specializes the [ion charge-state momentum convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) to the poloidal-momentum channel and is not the ion charge state's bulk poloidal flow velocity. The convective contribution to the momentum-flux closure is defined by: $$ \Pi_{s,\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{conv}} = V_{s,\mathrm p}\,g_{s,\mathrm p} $$ where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state, $\mathrm p$ denotes the poloidal momentum component, $\Pi_{s,\mathrm p}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is its convective flux through an oriented surface, $g_{s,\mathrm p}$ is its local momentum density, and $V_{s,\mathrm p}$ is this effective convection coefficient. The poloidal direction is tangent to a magnetic flux surface within a plane containing the toroidal symmetry axis. The poloidal label identifies the transported momentum component; it does not independently specify the direction through which that momentum is transported. The positive flux direction must therefore be specified by the oriented transport surface. This coefficient applies to one charge state, without summation or averaging over charge states. It excludes the gradient-driven diffusive contribution described by [poloidal ion charge-state momentum diffusivity], as well as separately represented residual stress and external momentum sources. Sign convention: Positive when positive poloidal momentum is convected along the positive normal of the oriented transport surface.

items.name: external_magnetic_flux
items.description: External magnetic flux is the signed surface integral of the magnetic field generated by sources outside the plasma current distribution over an oriented surface.
items.documentation: External magnetic flux is the signed surface integral of the magnetic field generated by sources outside the plasma current distribution over an oriented surface. It is the source-separated member of the [magnetic flux](name:magnetic_flux) family. The defining surface integral is: $$ \Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(S) = \int_S \mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ext}} \cdot d\mathbf{A} $$ where $\Phi_{\mathrm{ext}}(S)$ is the external magnetic flux associated with the oriented surface $S$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{ext}}$ is the magnetic-field vector produced by sources outside the plasma current distribution, and $d\mathbf{A}$ is the oriented surface-area element. The scope is the external-source contribution integrated over the complete surface specified by a concrete specialization. At this parent level, no poloidal or toroidal projection, spatial locus, or averaging weight is imposed; the quantity is a signed surface aggregate, not a local magnetic-field value, a flux-surface average, or a contribution generated by the plasma current itself. The child [average external magnetic flux](name:average_external_magnetic_flux) is a concrete poloidal specialization with averaging over the plasma cross-section. The related [current-weighted average external magnetic flux](name:current_weighted_average_external_magnetic_flux) uses plasma-current weighting for that aggregation; both remain source-separated instances of external magnetic flux. Sign convention: Positive when the net external magnetic field points along the positive normal of the oriented integration surface in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description: Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local angular-momentum transfer rate to bulk thermal electrons from Coulomb collisions with counter-passing fast particles.
items.documentation: Counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population, restricted to collisions with counter-passing fast particles. $$ \boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,cp}} = \left.\frac{\partial \boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll,cp}} $$ Here $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,cp}}$ is the collisional torque-density vector deposited in thermal electrons, and $\boldsymbol{\ell}_{e,\mathrm{th}}$ is their angular-momentum density. The subscript $\mathrm{cp}$ restricts the transfer to counter-passing fast particles. This quantity is an orbit-resolved contribution to the [thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions); its [toroidal counter-passing thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_counter_passing_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) is the toroidal projection, while the [toroidal thermal electron torque density due to collisions](name:toroidal_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) resolves the corresponding axis component without this orbit restriction. Contributions deposited in fast electrons and torque from non-Coulomb processes are excluded. Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component points along the corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame: increasing $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, or increasing $Z$.

items.name: logarithm_of_density
items.description: Logarithm of a selected plasma density, representing the natural-log transform of that density relative to a specified reference for the same density quantity. It is the base logarithmic density quantity from which coordinate derivatives may be formed.
items.documentation: Logarithm of density is the natural logarithm of a selected plasma density after normalization by a reference value for the same density quantity. It represents the logarithmic density variable itself, not a spatial derivative or gradient. The defining logarithmic transform is $$ L_n = \ln\!\left(\frac{n}{n_\mathrm{ref}}\right) $$ where $L_n$ is the logarithm of density, $n$ is the selected plasma density, and $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is the reference value used for the same selected density. The scope covers the logarithmic transform for any explicitly selected density population or component; a more specific standard name supplies the particular population, coordinate dependence, or reference convention. It excludes the density $n$ itself, a density ratio before applying the logarithm, and any coordinate derivative or gradient of $L_n$. A derivative specialization such as [logarithmic-density derivative with respect to normalized minor radius](name:derivative_of_logarithm_of_density_with_respect_to_normalized_minor_radius) denotes a derivative of $L_n$, not $L_n$ itself. For any coordinate $x$, the corresponding logarithmic derivative is $dL_n/dx = (1/n)\,dn/dx$ when $n_\mathrm{ref}$ is independent of $x$, where $x$ is the coordinate of differentiation.

items.name: power_due_to_recombination
items.description: Power deposited on plasma-facing materials by recombination processes, encompassing both plasma-ion recombination and surface recombination of neutral atoms, without restriction to a particular surface location.
items.documentation: Recombination power is the heat load delivered to plasma-facing materials when ions recover electrons and transition to neutral states, releasing ionization potential energy and residual kinetic energy at or near material surfaces. Two principal channels contribute: sheath-accelerated plasma-ion recombination at target surfaces, and surface recombination of neutral atoms into molecules, which deposits the molecular binding energy directly into the wall or divertor plate material. The integrated power from recombination events over a wetted area $A$ is: $$P_\text{rec} = \sum_s \int_A \Gamma_s \, E_s \, dA$$ where $\Gamma_s$ m$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$ is the incident particle flux density for species $s$ and $E_s$ [J] is the energy released per recombination event for that species, including ionization potential and kinetic contributions. This power channel is intrinsically non-negative and becomes particularly significant in detached and partially detached divertor regimes, where volumetric ion-electron recombination upstream of the strike point redistributes energy deposition away from the target. Location-specific realizations include [power deposited on a single divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination), the [total over the full divertor assembly](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination), and power at first-wall surfaces. The neutral recombination particle flux produced in these processes is characterized by [neutral_energy_flux_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_energy_flux_at_wall_due_to_recombination).

items.name: toroidal_magnetization_of_ferritic_element
items.description: Toroidal component of the ferritic-element magnetization vector: the signed projection of the effective magnetization assigned to a discrete ferritic element onto the positive toroidal direction in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. This is the element-level convention, not a pointwise bulk-material magnetization field.
items.documentation: Toroidal component of the ferritic-element magnetization vector is the signed projection of the effective magnetization assigned to a discrete ferritic element onto the toroidal basis direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The projection is defined by: $$ M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}} = \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{fe}} \cdot \hat{\phi} $$ where $\mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{fe}}$ is the ferritic-element magnetization vector assigned to the element, $\hat{\phi}$ is the unit vector in the direction of increasing toroidal angle, and $M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}}$ is this toroidal component. In this family, ferritic-element magnetization denotes the effective magnetization attributed to the individual ferritic element for its magnetic source strength. It is not the pointwise bulk magnetization field inside the material, and it is distinct from material properties such as magnetic permeability. Together with the [radial component](name:radial_magnetization_of_ferritic_element) and [vertical component](name:vertical_magnetization_of_ferritic_element), it forms the three cylindrical components of the same effective ferritic-element magnetization vector. Sign convention: Positive when $M_\phi^{\mathrm{fe}}$ points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ (counter-clockwise viewed from above $+\hat{Z}$).

items.name: total_electron_count
items.description: Total inventory of free electrons within the plasma, including thermal and fast populations and excluding electrons bound in atoms or molecules.
items.documentation: The total free-electron count is the number of unbound electrons contained within the plasma volume, aggregated over all electron populations. $$ N_e = \int_V n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV $$ where $N_e$ is the total free-electron count, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local [total electron density](name:total_electron_density), $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $dV$ is the differential volume element, and $V$ is the plasma volume. This quantity includes thermal, fast, and other free-electron populations present within $V$ and sums them over the entire plasma volume. It excludes electrons bound in neutral atoms or molecules and is distinct from local or volume-averaged density, which describes electrons per physical volume rather than the integrated inventory. The count is obtained by integrating the complete local electron density; a [line-averaged electron density](name:line_averaged_electron_density) represents a chord average and cannot substitute for this volume integral.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_oxygen_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density for the plasma, with oxygen summed over ionized charge states and neutral oxygen excluded.
items.documentation: Volume-averaged oxygen ion density relative to volume-averaged electron density is a scalar oxygen impurity fraction for the plasma. It compares the charge-state-summed volume average of ionized oxygen number density with the corresponding volume average of electron number density over the same averaging volume. The ratio is defined by $$ f_O = \frac{\left\langle \sum_{q=1}^{8} n_{O^{q+}} \right\rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V} $$ where $f_O$ is this oxygen-to-electron density ratio, $\langle\cdot\rangle_V$ denotes a volume average over the averaging volume $V$, $q$ is the oxygen charge-state index, $n_{O^{q+}}$ is the local number density of oxygen ions in charge state $q+$, and $n_e$ is the local electron number density. The denominator $\langle n_e\rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density). The numerator is summed over ionized oxygen charge states $O^{1+}$ through $O^{8+}$ and excludes neutral oxygen. This quantity is a single scalar composition fraction formed from volume-averaged populations; it is distinct from a local [oxygen density](name:oxygen_density), from a [line-averaged oxygen density](name:line_averaged_oxygen_density), and from a neutral-inclusive [volume-averaged oxygen density](name:volume_averaged_oxygen_density) when that quantity includes neutral oxygen. The essential relationship is normalization: the charge-state-summed volume-averaged oxygen ion density is divided by the [volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), so the result represents oxygen ion abundance relative to the electron population rather than an absolute density.

items.name: accumulated_total_prefill_gas_count
items.description: Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of all gas species introduced by injection during the plasma prefill phase, summed over species.
items.documentation: This quantity is the total gas inventory accumulated during the plasma prefill phase, expressed as an equivalent-electron count and summed over all injected species. It represents the integrated amount introduced before plasma breakdown, rather than an instantaneous injection rate. The accumulated equivalent-electron count is defined by $$ N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = \sum_s \int_{t_0}^{\min(t,t_1)} \dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{eq}}(t')\,dt' $$ where $s$ indexes injected gas species, $\dot{N}_{s,\mathrm{eq}}$ is the equivalent-electron injection rate of species $s$, $t_0$ and $t_1$ delimit the prefill phase, and $t$ is the evaluation time. The sum includes all species; a species-specific quantity such as [accumulated hydrogen prefill count](name:accumulated_hydrogen_prefill_count) is a component of this total. The quantity is distinct from the instantaneous injection rate and from inventories restricted to one species, while [accumulated prefill gas count](name:accumulated_prefill_gas_count) denotes the near-equivalent total inventory.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description: Fick's-law proportionality coefficient relating the density-normalized radial diffusive thermal energy flux of a specified ion charge state to its local temperature gradient.
items.documentation: The ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient in the radial direction quantifies gradient-driven diffusive transport of thermal energy carried by ions in one specified charge state. It is the radial directional specialization of the [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient), applying to the component along increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The defining relation for the density-normalized radial diffusive energy flux of charge state $z$ is: $$ \frac{Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}}{n_{i,z}} = -D_{i,z,E,R}\,\frac{\partial T_{i,z}}{\partial R} $$ where $Q_{i,z,\mathrm{diff},R}$ is the radial component of the diffusive thermal energy flux carried by ions in charge state $z$, $n_{i,z}$ is their number density, $T_{i,z}$ is their [temperature](name:ion_charge_state_temperature), and $D_{i,z,E,R}$ is this radial diffusion coefficient. The minus sign denotes radial transport down the local radial temperature gradient. This quantity applies to one specified ion charge state and is not an aggregation over charge states. It excludes convective, advective, and $E \times B$ contributions to the total ion heat flux; the charge-state-aggregated [ion energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) is a density-weighted mean over all ion species and charge states. Other directional specializations include the [parallel ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:parallel_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) and the [poloidal ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:poloidal_ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient).

items.name: toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the mode-n toroidal plasma-velocity perturbation in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame. It is the φ component of a single toroidal Fourier harmonic and is not the equilibrium toroidal flow.
items.documentation: The imaginary part of the complex amplitude of the mode-$n$ toroidal plasma-velocity perturbation is the coefficient of $i$ in the toroidal component of the first-order plasma velocity perturbation for a single toroidal Fourier harmonic. The toroidal component is the projection onto $\hat{\phi}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. It is a perturbation eigenfunction component, not the equilibrium toroidal flow. For a harmonic with phase dependence proportional to $e^{i(n\phi-\omega t)}$, the full complex toroidal component combines this quantity with the matched real part [toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part](name:toroidal_perturbed_plasma_velocity_real_part): $$ \delta \hat{v}_{\phi,n}(R,Z) = \delta \hat{\mathbf{v}}_n(R,Z)\cdot\hat{\phi} = \operatorname{Re}\!\left[\delta \hat{v}_{\phi,n}(R,Z)\right] + i\,\operatorname{Im}\!\left[\delta \hat{v}_{\phi,n}(R,Z)\right] $$ where $\delta \hat{\mathbf{v}}_n$ is the complex first-order velocity amplitude for toroidal mode number $n$, $\delta \hat{v}_{\phi,n}$ is its toroidal projection, $\omega$ is the mode angular frequency in the phase factor, and $i$ is the imaginary unit. This quantity is defined for one specified toroidal mode number $n$; contributions from other toroidal harmonics are excluded. A global phase rotation of the eigenfunction changes the split between real and imaginary parts, so this component must be interpreted with the matched real part and the chosen eigenfunction phase reference. Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary coefficient of the toroidal velocity perturbation is directed along $\hat{\phi}$, the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: outer_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil
items.description: Nonnegative distance from the annulus center to the outer conducting boundary of a poloidal field coil's annular conductor cross-section.
items.documentation: The outer [radius](name:radius) is the larger of the two radii bounding the annular conductor cross-section of one poloidal field coil. It extends from the common annulus center to the outer conducting boundary. The outer radius is defined by $$ R_{\mathrm{out}} = \left\|\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{b}}-\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{c}}\right\| $$ where $R_{\mathrm{out}}$ is the outer radius, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{b}}$ is the position of any point on the outer conducting boundary, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{c}}$ is the annulus-center position, and $\|\cdot\|$ denotes Euclidean distance within the cross-sectional plane. The [inner radius](name:inner_radius_of_poloidal_field_coil) bounds the central aperture. Together, the inner radius, outer radius, and center position specify the annulus geometry. For a nondegenerate conducting annulus, $0 \leq R_{\mathrm{in}} < R_{\mathrm{out}}$, where $R_{\mathrm{in}}$ is the inner radius. This quantity describes one annular cross-section, not the coil's distance from the machine symmetry axis. It is distinct from the [circular-segment curvature radius](name:radius_of_poloidal_field_coil), which describes an arc of the coil cross-sectional contour.

items.name: poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_imaginary_part
items.description: Imaginary component of the complex poloidal projection, along the increasing-θ tangent in flux coordinates (ρ, θ, φ), of the first-order magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma boundary for a specified toroidal Fourier mode.
items.documentation: Imaginary component of the complex poloidal projection, along the increasing-$\theta$ tangent in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, of the first-order magnetic-field perturbation eigenfunction in the current-free vacuum region outside the plasma boundary for a specified toroidal Fourier mode. It is a signed scalar magnetic-field amplitude of the complex vacuum perturbation. The complex poloidal vacuum perturbation amplitude is decomposed into real and imaginary parts by: $$ \delta B_{\theta}^{(V)}(\rho,\theta;n) = \operatorname{Re}\{\delta B_{\theta}^{(V)}(\rho,\theta;n)\} + i\,\operatorname{Im}\{\delta B_{\theta}^{(V)}(\rho,\theta;n)\} $$ where $\delta B_{\theta}^{(V)}$ is the component of $\delta\mathbf{B}^{(V)}$ along the unit poloidal tangent $\hat{e}_{\theta}=(\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta)_{\rho,\phi}/|(\partial\mathbf{x}/\partial\theta)_{\rho,\phi}|$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $\rho$ is the selected magnetic-flux-surface label, $\theta$ is the poloidal angle, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, $n$ is the integer toroidal Fourier mode number, $i$ is the imaginary unit, and $\operatorname{Re}$ and $\operatorname{Im}$ denote the real-part and imaginary-part operators. The quantity named here is $\operatorname{Im}\{\delta B_{\theta}^{(V)}\}$, and all magnetic-field amplitudes in the equation have units of tesla. The superscript $V$ denotes the vacuum-region perturbation and excludes perturbations in the plasma region. In that region the first-order perturbation is current-free and solenoidal, satisfying $\nabla\times\delta\mathbf{B}^{(V)}=0$ and $\nabla\cdot\delta\mathbf{B}^{(V)}=0$. This quantity is paired with [poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part](name:poloidal_perturbed_vacuum_magnetic_field_real_part); a common complex rescaling of a linear eigenfunction changes absolute amplitude and phase but not the component identity defined here. Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary part of the poloidal projection is directed along the unit tangent for increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: nuclear_power_density_of_limiter_tile
items.description: Local volumetric rate of nuclear energy deposition in limiter-tile material from neutron interactions and associated absorption of primary and secondary gamma radiation.
items.documentation: Nuclear power density of a limiter tile is the local volumetric energy deposition rate within the material of one limiter tile caused by neutron interactions and associated gamma-radiation absorption. It is the nuclear contribution to the broader power density of a limiter tile, not the total local energy source. $$ P_{\mathrm{nuc}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{tile}}} q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V $$ where $q_{\mathrm{nuc}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the nuclear power density at position $\mathbf{r}$, $V_{\mathrm{tile}}$ is the material volume of the limiter tile, and $P_{\mathrm{nuc}}$ is the corresponding [nuclear power of a limiter tile](name:nuclear_heating_power_of_limiter_tile). The quantity includes energy deposited volumetrically by neutron scattering and capture and by absorption of primary and secondary gamma radiation. Surface heat loads, externally applied heating, and nonnuclear energy-transfer mechanisms are excluded.

items.name: total_neutral_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection
items.description: Instantaneous equivalent-electron source rate of neutral gas introduced into the vessel by gas injection, summed over all injected species.
items.documentation: This quantity is the instantaneous neutral-gas throughput supplied to the vessel by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron rate. It combines all injected neutral species rather than representing one gas species. For the set of injected species, the equivalent-electron rate is defined by: $$ \dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}} = \sum_{s \in \mathcal{S}} Z_s\,\dot{N}_s $$ where $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the total equivalent-electron source rate, $\mathcal{S}$ is the set of injected neutral gas species, $\dot{N}_s$ is the particle injection rate of species $s$, and $Z_s$ is the equivalent-electron weighting per injected particle. For an atomic species, $Z_s$ is its atomic number; for a molecule, it is the sum of the atomic numbers of its constituent atoms. The quantity applies to the vessel-level gas input and is aggregated by summing over all injected neutral species. It is an instantaneous rate, not a time-integrated inventory, and excludes ionization and subsequent plasma particle sources. Species-resolved rates such as the [hydrogen source rate due to gas injection](name:hydrogen_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection) provide individual contributions to this total. Unlike the [total lower gas source rate of the vacuum vessel due to gas injection](name:total_lower_gas_source_rate_of_vacuum_vessel_due_to_gas_injection), it is not restricted to the lower vessel region. The corresponding accumulated quantity, such as the [accumulated hydrogen count due to gas injection](name:accumulated_hydrogen_count_due_to_gas_injection), is obtained by time integration and represents delivered inventory rather than instantaneous throughput.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top
items.description: Dimensionless toroidal-flux label locating the top of the H-mode edge pedestal on a nested magnetic surface relative to the magnetic axis and last closed flux surface.
items.documentation: The normalized toroidal flux coordinate evaluated at the pedestal top is the dimensionless magnetic-surface label assigned to the top of the H-mode edge pedestal. It locates that position within the nested closed-flux-surface family, rather than representing a cylindrical distance or a local vector component. For a nested equilibrium, the coordinate is defined by $$ \rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ped}) = \left[\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{ped}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{axis})}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{LCFS}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(\mathrm{axis})}\right]^{1/2} $$ where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(\mathrm{ped})$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the pedestal top, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by a magnetic surface, $\mathrm{ped}$ denotes the pedestal-top position, $\mathrm{axis}$ denotes the magnetic axis, and $\mathrm{LCFS}$ denotes the last closed flux surface. The value applies specifically at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal, the inner shoulder of the edge transport barrier. Its position is defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). This is a single coordinate evaluation: no species, charge-state, or population aggregation applies, and no surface averaging is implied. It is distinct from a cylindrical radial distance and from the unnormalized [toroidal flux coordinate at the pedestal top](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_pedestal_top). This entry is the pedestal-top specialization of the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), with the same axis-to-boundary normalization. It should not be interpreted as the corresponding [normalized poloidal flux coordinate](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate), which labels surfaces using poloidal rather than toroidal magnetic flux.

items.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
