items.description: Signed coordinate of a neutral beam injector source-outline vertex along the injector’s first local tangential direction.
items.documentation: This quantity is the signed first local tangential coordinate of a point on a neutral beam injector source outline. It belongs to the injector’s object-local frame and is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector) to describe the outline in its tangent plane. The coordinate is defined by $$ x_1 = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_1 $$ where $x_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position of the source-outline vertex, $\mathbf{r}_0$ is the origin of the injector-local frame, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ is its positive first local tangential unit vector. The origin and orientation are determined by the neutral beam injector’s local geometric convention; this quantity is not a coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame and does not specify that convention by itself. Sign convention: Positive when the outline vertex lies in the direction of the positive first local tangential basis vector from the local-frame origin.

items.name: normalized_gyrocenter_perturbed_density
items.description: Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter-density fluctuation response, distinct from a gyroaveraged particle-density perturbation.
items.documentation: Normalized gyrocenter perturbed density is the species-resolved zeroth velocity-space moment of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution divided by a positive reference density. It is the before-finite-Larmor-radius gyrocenter density fluctuation response; the normalization removes the scale of the reference density while preserving perturbation amplitude and phase. For magnetic moment $\mu = m_s v_\perp^2/(2B)$, the normalized moment is defined by: $$ \widehat{n}_{gc,s} = \frac{1}{n_{\mathrm{ref},s}} \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} \int_{0}^{\infty} \delta f_{gc,s}(v_\parallel,\mu)\,\frac{2\pi B}{m_s}\,d\mu\,dv_\parallel $$ where $\widehat{n}_{gc,s}$ is the normalized gyrocenter perturbed density for species $s$, $n_{\mathrm{ref},s}$ is the positive reference number density for that species, $\delta f_{gc,s}$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution with respect to ordinary velocity-space volume, $B$ is the local magnetic-field magnitude, $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\parallel$ is velocity parallel to the magnetic field, $v_\perp$ is speed perpendicular to the magnetic field, and $\mu$ is magnetic moment. The factor $2\pi B/m_s$ is the gyroangle-integrated velocity-space Jacobian for this definition of $\mu$. For a species represented by multiple charge states, the perturbed gyrocenter-density numerator and the reference density are charge-state-summed before the ratio is formed. This quantity excludes any Bessel-function or finite-Larmor-radius weighting inside the velocity-space integral; that weighted moment is the normalized gyrocenter gyroaveraged density. The dimensional numerator of the ratio is the unnormalized gyrocenter-density perturbation; the related perturbed gyrocenter density denotes a dimensionless gyrocenter-density perturbation in the same family. The normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure is the corresponding perturbed pressure moment. For complex perturbation amplitudes, the integral is taken over the complex amplitude; the arbitrary overall mode phase is external to the definition. Sign convention: Positive when, for a real perturbation amplitude, the velocity-space integral of the perturbed gyrocenter distribution gives an excess gyrocenter density relative to the positive reference density.

items.name: volumetric_force
items.description: Electromagnetic Lorentz body-force density vector acting locally on plasma, conducting wall, or structural material, with components resolved in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation: The volumetric force is the local electromagnetic Lorentz force density acting on plasma and current-carrying conducting or structural material. Its projections include the [radial volumetric force](name:radial_volumetric_force), [toroidal volumetric force](name:toroidal_volumetric_force), and [vertical volumetric force](name:vertical_volumetric_force). The electromagnetic force density is defined by $$ \mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{vol}} = \rho_e \mathbf{E} + \mathbf{J} \times \mathbf{B} $$ where $\mathbf{f}_{\mathrm{vol}}$ is the volumetric force vector, $\rho_e$ is charge density, $\mathbf{E}$ is electric field, $\mathbf{J}$ is current density, and $\mathbf{B}$ is magnetic field. The quantity is local and is distinct from the net force obtained by integrating it over a material volume. Sign convention: Positive when a force component points along its corresponding positive basis direction—increasing $R$, increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, or increasing $Z$—in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis
items.description: Temperature of electrons at the magnetic axis measures their local mean random kinetic energy per particle, excluding coherent electron flow.
items.documentation: Temperature of electron at magnetic axis The nonrelativistic defining relation is $$ T_{e,\mathrm{axis}} = \frac{2}{3}\left\langle E_{e,\mathrm{random}}\right\rangle_{\mathrm{axis}} $$ where $T_{e,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the electron temperature at the magnetic axis, $E_{e,\mathrm{random}}$ is the electron kinetic energy relative to the local mean electron flow, and the angle brackets denote a particle-number-weighted average over the local electron population. The subscript $\mathrm{axis}$ denotes evaluation at the magnetic axis. This quantity is a local value, not a volume average or a maximum over the plasma. It specializes [temperature at the magnetic axis](name:temperature_at_magnetic_axis) to the electron kinetic temperature, unlike [radiative temperature at the magnetic axis](name:radiative_temperature_at_magnetic_axis), which represents radiation brightness. It forms the numerator of the [ratio of on-axis to volume-averaged electron temperature](name:ratio_of_electron_temperature_at_magnetic_axis_to_volume_averaged_electron_temperature). That ratio expresses central temperature peaking relative to the electron-temperature volume average inside the last closed magnetic flux surface. The closed magnetic-field line about which nested toroidal magnetic flux surfaces are arranged. Where $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}(R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}) = 0$, $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is poloidal magnetic field; $R_{\mathrm{axis}}, Z_{\mathrm{axis}}$ is the O-point inside the nested closed flux surfaces.

items.name: line_averaged_tungsten_density
items.description: Line-of-sight average of the number density of positively charged tungsten ions, summed over all ionization states and excluding neutral tungsten.
items.documentation: This quantity is the line-of-sight average of the charge-state-summed number density of positively charged tungsten ions. $$ \bar n_{\mathrm{W}} = \frac{1}{L}\int_{\mathcal{L}} \left[\sum_{Z=1}^{74} n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)\right] \, dl $$ Here, $\bar n_{\mathrm{W}}$ is the line-averaged tungsten-ion number density, $\mathcal{L}$ is the specified averaging line, $L$ is its total length, $l$ is distance along that line, $Z$ is the positive tungsten charge-state index, and $n_{\mathrm{W}^{Z+}}(l)$ is the local number density of tungsten ions in charge state $Z$. The sum includes all positive tungsten ionization states and excludes neutral tungsten. The quantity applies to the aggregate tungsten-ion population along the specified line and is averaged over that line rather than evaluated locally or averaged over volume. It therefore differs from the local or otherwise spatially averaged [tungsten-ion density](name:tungsten_density) by its line-of-sight aggregation, and from [volume-averaged tungsten density](name:volume_averaged_tungsten_density) by using a line rather than the enclosed plasma volume.

items.name: tritium_density
items.description: Local number density of tritium ions in the plasma, the foundational fuel-ion parameter underlying chord-averaged, volume-averaged, and isotopic ratio child quantities.
items.documentation: Tritium ion number density $n_T$ quantifies the local concentration of hydrogen-3 fuel ions in the plasma. It serves as the common physical basis for a family of derived quantities: the chord-integrated mean [line_averaged_tritium_density](name:line_averaged_tritium_density), the confined-volume mean [volume_averaged_tritium_density](name:volume_averaged_tritium_density), and dimensionless isotopic ratios such as ratio_of_tritium_density_to_electron_density and [ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density](name:ratio_of_tritium_density_to_deuterium_density). In deuterium-tritium (DT) fusion plasmas the local volumetric reaction rate is: $$ R_{DT} = n_T \, n_D \langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT} $$ where $n_D$ is the deuterium ion number density and $\langle \sigma v \rangle_{DT}$ is the Maxwellian-averaged DT fusion reactivity. The combined DT fuel-ion purity relative to the electron population is tracked by ratio_of_deuterium_tritium_density_to_electron_density. Tritium density is inferred from active charge-exchange recombination spectroscopy, neutron emission measurements in DT plasmas, or pellet injection and fueling diagnostics.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_boron_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description: Dimensionless global boron abundance ratio using separately volume-averaged boron and electron number densities, with neutral boron and every ionic charge state included.
items.documentation: This quantity is the global abundance of elemental boron relative to the electron population. It characterizes plasma composition over the full plasma volume rather than at a local point or along a line of sight. The defining ratio is $$ f_B = \frac{\overline{n}_B}{\overline{n}_e} $$ where $f_B$ is the boron-to-electron abundance ratio, $\overline{n}_B$ is the volume-averaged elemental boron number density, and $\overline{n}_e$ is the volume-averaged electron number density. The overbar denotes averaging over the plasma volume. The numerator includes neutral boron and every ionic boron charge state, while the denominator represents the complete electron population. For the associated plasma-composition convention, the ratio is evaluated at the time of peak electron density. This quantity is distinct from local [boron density](name:boron_density) and from [line-averaged boron density](name:line_averaged_boron_density): it is a quotient of two separately volume-averaged densities, not a volume average of a pointwise ratio or a line average. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged boron density](name:volume_averaged_boron_density), making this ratio the corresponding normalized composition measure.

items.name: normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_heat_flux_bessel_1
items.description: Normalized first-Bessel-weighted parallel heat-flux moment of a perturbed gyrocenter distribution in a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode.
items.documentation: This quantity represents the energy-weighted parallel motion carried by the perturbed gyrocenter population. It is evaluated in the field-aligned parallel direction and includes first-order Bessel weighting. The normalized moment is defined by $$ \widehat{q}_{\parallel,J_1}=\frac{1}{\mathcal{N}_q}\int \frac{1}{2}m v_{\parallel}v^2 J_1\,\delta f_g^{(1)}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $\widehat{q}_{\parallel,J_1}$ is the normalized parallel heat-flux moment, $\mathcal{N}_q$ is the normalization factor for the corresponding heat-flux moment, $m$ is the gyrocenter particle mass, $v_{\parallel}$ is the velocity component parallel to the magnetic field, $v$ is the particle-speed magnitude, $J_1$ is the first-order Bessel weighting factor at the prescribed gyrokinetic argument, $\delta f_g^{(1)}(\mathbf{v})$ is the perturbed gyrocenter distribution function, $\mathbf{v}$ is the velocity-space coordinate, and $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element. The integral applies to the perturbed gyrocenter distribution associated with a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode and aggregates the represented distribution over velocity space. It excludes the equilibrium or unperturbed distribution and is not an unweighted heat-flux moment. The parallel projection distinguishes this quantity from the perpendicular heat-flux moment perpendicular gyrocenter heat perturbed flux normalized of gyrokinetic eigenmode. It belongs to the same first-Bessel-weighted perturbed gyrocenter moment family as [normalized perturbed parallel gyrocenter current density bessel 1](name:normalized_perturbed_parallel_gyrocenter_current_density_bessel_1), but uses the energy-weighted heat-flux kernel rather than the current-density kernel.

items.name: co_passing_fast_current_density
items.description: Co-passing fast-particle current density is the signed conventional electric-charge flux per unit area carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped guiding-center orbits. It is a vector orbit-class contribution and excludes compensating electron and thermal-ion return currents.
items.documentation: Co-passing fast-particle current density is the signed conventional charge-flux density carried by fast particles on co-passing, untrapped guiding-center orbits. It is the co-passing orbit-class contribution to [current density](name:current_density), not the sum over all fast-particle orbit classes. The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment restricted to the co-passing orbit class: $$ \mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{fast,co}}(\mathbf{x},t)=\sum_{s\in\mathrm{fast}} q_s \int_{\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{co}}} \mathbf{v}\, f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\, d^3v $$ where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes included fast-particle species, $q_s$ is the particle charge of species $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $f_s$ is the velocity-space distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the velocity-space subset whose guiding-center orbit invariants classify the particle as co-passing. Specific scalar components, such as [toroidal co-passing fast current density](name:toroidal_co_passing_fast_current_density), are projections of this vector; the vector quantity itself is not limited to the $\hat{\phi}$ projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It is distinct from [counter-passing fast current density](name:counter_passing_fast_current_density) and [trapped fast current density](name:trapped_fast_current_density). Compensating electron and thermal-ion return-current contributions are excluded; they belong to other components of the total current density. Sign convention: Positive when the selected scalar projection of the co-passing fast-particle charge flux is aligned with the positive direction defining that projection.

items.name: triangularity_of_flux_surface
items.description: Signed dimensionless shape parameter measuring the normalized horizontal displacement of a nested magnetic flux surface’s upper or lower vertical extremum.
items.documentation: Triangularity of a nested magnetic flux surface is the signed shape parameter formed from the horizontal displacement of an upper or lower vertical extremum, normalized by the surface’s horizontal half-width. For a selected upper or lower vertical extremum, triangularity is defined in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame by $$ \delta_s = \frac{R_c - R_s}{a} $$ where $\delta_s$ is the triangularity, $s$ identifies the selected upper or lower vertical extremum, $R_s$ is its radial coordinate, $R_c$ is the radial midpoint of the flux surface’s horizontal extent, and $a$ is the corresponding horizontal half-width. This is a geometric parameter of an individual nested magnetic flux surface in an equilibrium plasma. The unqualified quantity covers either vertical extremum and carries no aggregation over multiple flux surfaces, plasma volume, or the plasma boundary. Triangularity characterizes the radial displacement of a vertical extremum; it is distinct from [elongation of a flux surface](name:elongation_of_flux_surface), which describes the ratio of vertical to horizontal extent, and from [outer squareness of a flux surface](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface), which describes corner deformation. The upper and lower branch-specific quantities are [upper triangularity of a flux surface](name:upper_triangularity_of_flux_surface) and [lower triangularity of a flux surface](name:lower_triangularity_of_flux_surface); each is an instance of this parent quantity with $s$ fixed to the corresponding vertical extremum.

items.name: ion_energy_diffusivity
items.description: Effective coefficient linking an ion population's density-normalized diffusive heat flux to its temperature gradient, without prescribing a transport direction.
items.documentation: Ion energy diffusivity characterizes gradient-driven transport of thermal energy carried by an ion population. It specifies the effective proportionality between density-normalized diffusive heat flux and the corresponding temperature gradient, without selecting a transport direction or implying isotropic transport. For a chosen physical transport direction, the defining Fickian closure is: $$ \frac{Q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -k_{\mathrm{B}}D_{i,W}\frac{\partial T_i}{\partial \ell} $$ where $Q_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux component along that direction, $n_i$ is the ion population's number density, $D_{i,W}$ is its effective energy diffusivity, $T_i$ is its thermodynamic temperature, $\ell$ is physical distance along the selected direction, and $k_{\mathrm{B}}$ is Boltzmann's constant. The subscript $i$ denotes the ion population, and $W$ labels the energy channel. The minus sign makes positive diffusivity correspond to down-gradient transport. The population may comprise one ion species or collectively all ion species. Number density and diffusive heat flux are summed over all included ionic charge states and species, while temperature is their density-weighted mean. When the constituents share a common temperature, the effective diffusivity is their density-weighted mean diffusivity; otherwise it is defined by the combined flux–gradient closure rather than an unqualified average of constituent coefficients. This coefficient excludes convective and advective energy transport and is distinct from particle diffusivity. Electron and neutral heat transport are outside its scope. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead describes transport associated with one specified ionic charge state. The [parallel ion energy diffusivity](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusivity) specializes this definition to field-aligned transport for the collective ion population, whereas the [poloidal ion energy diffusivity](name:poloidal_ion_energy_diffusivity) specializes it to poloidal transport for a specified ion species.

items.name: accumulated_ammonia_count
items.description: Cumulative post-breakdown inventory of ammonia molecules introduced into the plasma vessel, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with ten count units assigned to each neutral NH3 molecule.
items.documentation: The accumulated ammonia count is the cumulative post-breakdown amount of NH3 introduced into the plasma vessel, represented using an equivalent-electron accounting convention. It is the post-breakdown component of the total ammonia count, not a direct count of free plasma electrons. $$ C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = (Z_\mathrm{N}+3Z_\mathrm{H})N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} = 10N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}} $$ Here, $C_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count, $N_{\mathrm{NH_3}}^{\mathrm{acc}}$ is the cumulative number of ammonia molecules introduced after plasma breakdown, and $Z_\mathrm{N}=7$ and $Z_\mathrm{H}=1$ are the atomic numbers of nitrogen and hydrogen. The quantity excludes ammonia introduced during prefill, which is represented by [ammonia prefill count](name:ammonia_prefill_count), and does not represent instantaneous injection rate, retained neutral inventory, ionization state, or actual free-electron content.

items.name: suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure
items.description: Kinetic pressure contributed by suprathermal neutral particles occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state, including anisotropic velocity-space contributions from the nonthermal population.
items.documentation: Suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure is the state-resolved anisotropic kinetic pressure of suprathermal neutral atoms or molecules occupying a specified internal quantum or excitation state. It is a partial pressure for the selected internal state and suprathermal population, not a sum over all internal states and not the thermal neutral contribution. For state $a$, the pressure tensor of the suprathermal population is the central second velocity-space moment: $$ \mathbf{P}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a = m_a \int (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) \otimes (\mathbf{v}-\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a) f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v $$ where $m_a$ is the particle mass, $f^{\mathrm{sup}}_a(\mathbf{v})$ is the velocity distribution of suprathermal neutrals in state $a$, $\mathbf{u}^{\mathrm{sup}}_a$ is the mean velocity of that selected population, and $\otimes$ denotes the dyadic product. The central moment excludes dynamic pressure from directed bulk flow. Directional or gyrotropic components are projections or averages of this tensor; for example, [perpendicular suprathermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:perpendicular_suprathermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the component transverse to the local magnetic field. [Thermal neutral internal-state pressure](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_pressure) is the corresponding thermal contribution, while [total neutral internal-state pressure](name:total_neutral_internal_state_pressure) combines thermal and suprathermal contributions for the same internal state.

items.name: inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description: Reciprocal square of total magnetic-field strength, providing a positive magnetic-geometry factor for equilibrium and flux-surface-averaged transport relations.
items.documentation: The inverse square of total magnetic-field strength is a local magnetic-geometry factor that increases as the total field weakens and remains positive wherever the field magnitude is nonzero. It is defined as the reciprocal of the [square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude): $$ B^{-2} = \frac{1}{B^2} = \frac{1}{\lvert \mathbf{B} \rvert^2} $$ where $\mathbf{B}$ is the total magnetic-field vector and $B$ is its magnitude. The quantity applies to the full magnetic field in an equilibrium plasma, including all vector components and without restriction to a particle population. At the parent level it is a local quantity with no flux-surface or volume aggregation; it is distinct from the squared field magnitude itself and from the reciprocal square of any selected field component. The [flux-surface-averaged inverse square of magnetic-field magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude) is obtained by applying a flux-surface average to this local factor. The averaging is a separate aggregation operation and does not alter the reciprocal-square transformation.
